# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

4b. **TTL decision for #5 below:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive /
    10s negative — verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new
    numbers. A tool's installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the
    cost of re-probing every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a
    longer, bespoke TTL isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.**
   `AgentRunner.classify`, `FileTreeModel`, and `RustJJProvider.runCLI` still read a killed
   child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed `claude` agent shows
   "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original gh-flap fix was meant to
   end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies `signaled`, so check order matters
   in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the mechanism is already shipped and tested.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** jj's template pre-quotes
    non-identifier names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted
    name always fails — tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a
    bookmark name. Parse names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name
    rather than reusing a pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.**
    `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no `primaryRemote` filter — with
    `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row read decides the counts while
    every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root cause lets `@..trunk()` count
    against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

## Also worth a look while touching this area

10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).

## Explicitly excluded, and why

- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — both explicitly scheduled by TODOS.md for
  *after* the GA tag; the pin bump entry says so in its own priority line.
- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — the entry itself flags
  "broad blast radius... needs its own careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix" and "no
  user-visible bug today." Wrong trade immediately before a tag.
- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — internal rewrite of the theme-apply path for
  zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine verification first. Pure regression risk.
- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its stated value is as the *pin bump's* tripwire;
  schedule it with that post-GA work, not before.
- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no user impact confirmed
  worth pre-GA churn (shielded by other invariants / uncommon and content is still shown,
  just on one side).
- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
  structured diff hunks, notification preferences/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme
  content additions, OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream anyway), memory diagnostics
  tooling, quick-switcher deferrals, search section for the activity bar. All real roadmap
  items, none are bugs in what's shipped.
- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item at all (external
  tooling/config), out of scope for this release regardless of cut depth.

  and `make cli-lint`.

   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** jj's template pre-quotes
    non-identifier names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted
    name always fails — tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a
    bookmark name. Parse names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name
    rather than reusing a pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.**
    `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no `primaryRemote` filter — with
    `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row read decides the counts while
    every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root cause lets `@..trunk()` count
    against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

# Test Plan
Generated by /plan-eng-review on 2026-08-09
Branch: master
Repo: workroom (Go CLI + macOS SwiftUI app)

## Affected Components (no web routes — CLI + native app)
- `internal/config` (CLI) — config lock contention under concurrent CLI/app writes
- `JJSnapshotGate` + status-sweep suppression (macapp) — fetch/pull vs. background status reads
- VCS toolbar Abort-rebase action (macapp) — colocated jj repo with a real git rebase-merge
- VCS toolbar action failures after a workroom is deleted mid-action (macapp)
- Git/jj tool-version warning banner (macapp) — after `brew upgrade git`/`jj`
- Agent run banner + file tree + jj CLI errors (macapp) — after killing/cancelling a run
- VCS toolbar Pull/branch tracking on jj projects with a feature-branch base, a quoted
  bookmark name, or multiple remotes tracking the same branch
- Terminal pane content with VoiceOver enabled (macapp)

## Key Interactions to Verify
- Run two `workroom` CLI commands (or CLI + app) against the same project concurrently;
  confirm neither corrupts `config.json`.
- Start a `pull --rebase` from one window while another window's background status sweep
  is active on the same project; confirm no `packed-refs.lock` contention.
- In a colocated jj+git root, run `git rebase` in a terminal to leave `rebase-merge` behind,
  then click the toolbar's Abort rebase; confirm it actually aborts.
- Delete a workroom while a VCS action is in flight against it; confirm the resulting toast
  names the real cause, not "git isn't on PATH".
- With git below the version floor, run `brew upgrade git`, wait for the cache TTL, and
  confirm fetch/push/pull re-enable without relaunching the app.
- Kill (⌘.) an in-flight Claude agent run; confirm the banner shows a killed/interrupted
  state, not "exit 9".
- On a jj project: create a workroom off a feature branch (not trunk), rename a bookmark to
  something needing jj-template quoting (e.g. contains `|`), and configure two remotes
  tracking the same branch — confirm Pull, tracking counts, and remote attribution are all
  correct in each case.
- Enable VoiceOver, focus a terminal pane, run a command, select text; confirm VoiceOver
  announces terminal content and the current selection.

## Edge Cases
- Config lock held by a process that then crashes (kill -9) mid-write — a new writer must
  still proceed, not wait forever or corrupt the file.
- `JJSnapshotGate` genuinely wedged predecessor (not just slow) — confirm the existing
  self-heal ceiling still applies unchanged for the truly-hung case, only the fetch/pull
  suppression is new.
- Non-colocated jj workspace (no `.git` at all) clicking Abort rebase — must still report
  "Nothing to abort" (this path must NOT regress).

## Critical Paths
- Two-window concurrent write to the same project's config and same project's `.git`
  (Tier 1 items #1 and #2) — these are the data-loss/corruption-risk items; verify first.

aiTitle: Prioritize todos for v2 final release

content.content:
1	# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
6	no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
7	most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
8	(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
9	content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
10	tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.
11	
12	What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
13	wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
14	GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
15	are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
16	the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
17	wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.
18	
19	No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
20	build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
21	flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
22	this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
23	three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
24	`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
25	agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
26	build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
27	unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
28	nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.
29	
30	## Landing shape
31	
32	10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
33	Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
34	terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
35	bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
36	— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
37	version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
38	tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
39	accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
40	revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
41	TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).
42	
43	## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)
44	
45	1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
46	   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
47	   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
48	   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
49	   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
50	   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
51	   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
52	   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
53	   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
54	   data-loss race.
55	   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
56	   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
57	   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
58	   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
59	   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
60	   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
61	   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
62	   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
63	   precedent in this codebase to lean on.
64	
65	2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
66	   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
67	   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
68	   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
69	   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
70	   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
71	   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
72	   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
73	   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
74	   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
75	   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
76	   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
77	   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
78	   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
79	   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
80	   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
81	   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
82	   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).
83	
84	## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix
85	
86	3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
87	   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
88	   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
89	   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
90	   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
91	   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
92	   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
93	   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
94	   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
95	   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
96	   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
97	   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
98	   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
99	   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.
100	
101	4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
102	   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
103	   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
104	   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.
105	
106	5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
107	   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
108	   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
109	   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
110	   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
111	   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
112	   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
113	   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
114	   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
115	   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
116	   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
117	   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.
118	
119	6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
120	   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
121	   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
122	   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
123	   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
124	   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
125	   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
126	   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
127	   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
128	   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
129	   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
130	   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
131	   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
132	   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.
133	
134	## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)
135	
136	7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
137	   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
138	   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
139	   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
140	   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.
141	
142	8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
143	   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
144	   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
145	   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
146	   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
147	   pre-joined display string.
148	
149	9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
150	   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
151	   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
152	   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
153	   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.
154	
155	## Also worth a look while touching this area
156	
157	10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
158	    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
159	    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
160	    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
161	    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
162	    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
163	    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
164	    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
165	    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).
166	
167	## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)
168	
169	- **`GitHubAuthCache`** (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`, 114 lines) — the freshness-lease +
170	  generation-stamped in-flight + instance-ownership shape item #5 lifts wholesale, including
171	  its exact TTL numbers.
172	- **`committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`**
173	  (`AppStore.swift:333-341`, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:655-677`) — the read-lane
174	  suppression pattern item #2's fetch/pull fix mirrors exactly.
175	- **`Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`** (`VCSWriting.swift:1090,1323`)
176	  — the colocated-rebase detection item #3 reuses instead of writing new branching logic.
177	- **`CommandResult.signaled`** (shipped, gh-flap fix) — item #6 wires three more consumers
178	  into a mechanism that already exists and is tested; it does not add a new one.
179	
180	## NOT in scope (considered, explicitly deferred)
181	
182	- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — scheduled by TODOS.md for after the GA tag.
183	- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — broad blast radius across every caller, "no
184	  user-visible bug today" per its own entry; wrong trade immediately before a landing push.
185	- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine
186	  verification first; pure regression risk.
187	- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its value is as the pin bump's tripwire; schedule
188	  with that post-GA work.
189	- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no confirmed user impact
190	  worth the churn right now.
191	- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
192	  structured diff hunks, notification prefs/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme content,
193	  OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream), memory diagnostics tooling, quick-switcher
194	  deferrals, activity-bar search. Roadmap items, not bugs in what's shipped.
195	- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item; out of scope
196	  regardless of cut depth.
197	- **A fourth `signaled` consumer in `VCSWriting.swift`** — checked, already fixed (see item
198	  #6's note); correctly excluded from that item's scope, not silently missed.
199	- **Hand-rolled PID-liveness locking (Go)** — considered as the fix for item #1, rejected in
200	  favor of an OS-level advisory-lock library; see item #1's fix decision.
201	- **Raising `JJSnapshotGate.defaultMaxChainWait`** — considered as the fix for item #2,
202	  rejected because it would slow every unrelated status probe on the project, not just the
203	  ones racing a live write; see item #2's fix decision.
204	
205	## Test coverage diagram
206

208	are bugs in shipped code, so by construction none has a passing regression test yet — that's

# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
   pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

## Also worth a look while touching this area

10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- **`GitHubAuthCache`** (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`, 114 lines) — the freshness-lease +
  generation-stamped in-flight + instance-ownership shape item #5 lifts wholesale, including
  its exact TTL numbers.
- **`committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`**
  (`AppStore.swift:333-341`, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:655-677`) — the read-lane
  suppression pattern item #2's fetch/pull fix mirrors exactly.
- **`Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`** (`VCSWriting.swift:1090,1323`)
  — the colocated-rebase detection item #3 reuses instead of writing new branching logic.
- **`CommandResult.signaled`** (shipped, gh-flap fix) — item #6 wires three more consumers
  into a mechanism that already exists and is tested; it does not add a new one.

## NOT in scope (considered, explicitly deferred)

- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — scheduled by TODOS.md for after the GA tag.
- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — broad blast radius across every caller, "no
  user-visible bug today" per its own entry; wrong trade immediately before a landing push.
- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine
  verification first; pure regression risk.
- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its value is as the pin bump's tripwire; schedule
  with that post-GA work.
- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no confirmed user impact
  worth the churn right now.
- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
  structured diff hunks, notification prefs/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme content,
  OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream), memory diagnostics tooling, quick-switcher
  deferrals, activity-bar search. Roadmap items, not bugs in what's shipped.
- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item; out of scope
  regardless of cut depth.
- **A fourth `signaled` consumer in `VCSWriting.swift`** — checked, already fixed (see item
  #6's note); correctly excluded from that item's scope, not silently missed.
- **Hand-rolled PID-liveness locking (Go)** — considered as the fix for item #1, rejected in
  favor of an OS-level advisory-lock library; see item #1's fix decision.
- **Raising `JJSnapshotGate.defaultMaxChainWait`** — considered as the fix for item #2,
  rejected because it would slow every unrelated status probe on the project, not just the
  ones racing a live write; see item #2's fix decision.

## Test coverage diagram

Existing test files per touched component, and the gap each plan item closes. All ten items
are bugs in shipped code, so by construction none has a passing regression test yet — that's
the GAP this table exists to close, not a surprise finding.

```
CODE PATHS                                                    EXISTING TESTS
[Tier 1]

  ├── [GAP] concurrent writers, one holds a live lock          config_extra_test.go,
  │         >10s (simulate slow fn) — other must NOT steal     canonicalpath_test.go,
  │         it and must NOT corrupt the write                  channel_test.go
  └── [GAP] crashed holder (killed mid-write) — a NEW writer    (none cover concurrent
            must still be able to proceed                        contention/staleness)

JJSnapshotGate.swift + AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift           JJSnapshotGateTests.swift
  ├── [★★★ TESTED] same-project calls never overlap             (6 tests, all pre-fix
  ├── [★★★ TESTED] different projects run concurrently            behavior — none exercise
  ├── [★★★ TESTED] chain self-heals past a wedged predecessor     the NEW fetch/pull
  └── [GAP] fetch/pull in flight suppresses the read lanes        suppression counters)
        isFetchingProject/isPullingProject will gate — needs
        new tests mirroring isCommitting's existing coverage

[Tier 2]
VCSWriting.swift — abortRebase (jj branch)                     VCSWritingTests.swift
  └── [GAP] colocated jj root with a real git rebase-merge      (117 tests; none named
        left behind — must run real abort, not fake success      Abort/rebase-in-progress)

StatusCommandRunner.swift — classify(commandNotFound)          (no dedicated test file
  └── [GAP] cwd-vanished launch failure must map to its own       found for this classifier)
        sentinel, distinct from .toolMissing

  ├── [★★  TESTED] absent tool not cached (existing fix)        (29 tests; TTL/reentrancy/
  ├── [GAP] .belowFloor clears after TTL without relaunch         generation-stamp behavior
  └── [GAP] concurrent probeJJ:true/false reentrancy doesn't       not yet covered — the
        downgrade a jj-aware verdict                               new GitHubAuthCache-shaped

THE PLAN:

# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
   pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

## Also worth a look while touching this area

10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- **`GitHubAuthCache`** (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`, 114 lines) — the freshness-lease +
  generation-stamped in-flight + instance-ownership shape item #5 lifts wholesale, including
  its exact TTL numbers.
- **`committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`**
  (`AppStore.swift:333-341`, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:655-677`) — the read-lane
  suppression pattern item #2's fetch/pull fix mirrors exactly.
- **`Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`** (`VCSWriting.swift:1090,1323`)
  — the colocated-rebase detection item #3 reuses instead of writing new branching logic.
- **`CommandResult.signaled`** (shipped, gh-flap fix) — item #6 wires three more consumers
  into a mechanism that already exists and is tested; it does not add a new one.

## NOT in scope (considered, explicitly deferred)

- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — scheduled by TODOS.md for after the GA tag.
- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — broad blast radius across every caller, "no
  user-visible bug today" per its own entry; wrong trade immediately before a landing push.
- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine
  verification first; pure regression risk.
- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its value is as the pin bump's tripwire; schedule
  with that post-GA work.
- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no confirmed user impact
  worth the churn right now.
- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
  structured diff hunks, notification prefs/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme content,
  OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream), memory diagnostics tooling, quick-switcher
  deferrals, activity-bar search. Roadmap items, not bugs in what's shipped.
- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item; out of scope
  regardless of cut depth.
- **A fourth `signaled` consumer in `VCSWriting.swift`** — checked, already fixed (see item
  #6's note); correctly excluded from that item's scope, not silently missed.

# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
   pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

## Also worth a look while touching this area

10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- **`GitHubAuthCache`** (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`, 114 lines) — the freshness-lease +
  generation-stamped in-flight + instance-ownership shape item #5 lifts wholesale, including
  its exact TTL numbers.
- **`committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`**
  (`AppStore.swift:333-341`, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:655-677`) — the read-lane
  suppression pattern item #2's fetch/pull fix mirrors exactly.
- **`Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`** (`VCSWriting.swift:1090,1323`)
  — the colocated-rebase detection item #3 reuses instead of writing new branching logic.
- **`CommandResult.signaled`** (shipped, gh-flap fix) — item #6 wires three more consumers
  into a mechanism that already exists and is tested; it does not add a new one.

## NOT in scope (considered, explicitly deferred)

- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — scheduled by TODOS.md for after the GA tag.
- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — broad blast radius across every caller, "no
  user-visible bug today" per its own entry; wrong trade immediately before a landing push.
- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine
  verification first; pure regression risk.
- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its value is as the pin bump's tripwire; schedule
  with that post-GA work.
- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no confirmed user impact
  worth the churn right now.
- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
  structured diff hunks, notification prefs/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme content,
  OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream), memory diagnostics tooling, quick-switcher
  deferrals, activity-bar search. Roadmap items, not bugs in what's shipped.
- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item; out of scope
  regardless of cut depth.
- **A fourth `signaled` consumer in `VCSWriting.swift`** — checked, already fixed (see item
  #6's note); correctly excluded from that item's scope, not silently missed.
- **Hand-rolled PID-liveness locking (Go)** — considered as the fix for item #1, rejected in
  favor of an OS-level advisory-lock library; see item #1's fix decision.
- **Raising `JJSnapshotGate.defaultMaxChainWait`** — considered as the fix for item #2,
  rejected because it would slow every unrelated status probe on the project, not just the
  ones racing a live write; see item #2's fix decision.

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Lane A (Go, independent): #1. Lane B (VCSWriting.swift, sequential): #3 -> #7 -> #8 -> #9 —
all four touch the same file. Lane C (independent Core files, parallel-safe): #2, #4, #5,
#6 — four different files with no shared state. Lane D (independent subsystem): #10.

## Implementation Tasks (T1-T10)

T1 (P1): CLI, replace config lock with gofrs/flock. T2 (P1): macapp, add
isFetchingProject/isPullingProject mirroring isCommitting. T3 (P2): macapp, fix abortRebase
jj branch to check rebaseInProgress. T4 (P2): macapp, give cwd-vanished launch failure its
