# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
   pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

102	## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

104	1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
105	   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
106	   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
107	   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
108	   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
109	   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
110	   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
111	   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
112	   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
113	   data-loss race.
114	   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
115	   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
116	   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
117	   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
118	   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
119	   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
120	   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
121	   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
122	   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

124	2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
125	   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
126	   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
127	   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
128	   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
129	   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
130	   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
131	   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
132	   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
133	   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
134	   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
135	   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
136	   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
137	   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
138	   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
139	   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
140	   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
141	   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

The old and new processes then hold unrelated locks. GA rollout needs a compatibility protocol, likely an OS lock plus refreshing the legacy lockfile until old clients are obsolete.

- **T1 assumes all mutations participate and reread under lock.** Advisory locking prevents nothing if any writer bypasses `withLock`, or if callers read configuration before acquiring the lock and later overwrite the complete file. Neither invariant is included in the audit or tests.

- **T7 is not a bug-sized fix.** An unbookmarked jj commit has no intrinsic “own base.” Remembering one requires defining provenance, persistence, migration for existing workrooms, bookmark deletion/renaming, remote changes, and history rewrites. The safer GA behavior is to report “no upstream” and disable Pull.

- **T5’s proposed cache architecture does not solve the cited race.** A generation-stamped slot still permits a `probeJJ: false` result to replace a jj-aware aggregate verdict unless results are keyed or Git and jj are cached independently. “Instance ownership” may also create inconsistent verdicts and duplicate probes across consumers.

- **T4 assumes an error distinction the process API may not provide.** Spawn commonly reports `ENOENT` for both a missing executable and a missing working directory. A new enum case is useless without resolving the executable first or performing an explicit cwd check; the latter remains racy.

- **T7–T9 are one upstream-identity problem, not three independent patches.** Filtering `trackingByName` does not fix revsets still using `trunk()`, whose configured target may be another remote. Define one structured `(bookmark, remote, target commit)` model and use it for counts, labels, fetch, and rebase.

- **The jj sequencing is backwards.** Safe raw-name representation and revset quoting are prerequisites for storing or selecting a base. Implementing T7 before T8/T9 invites immediate rework and can persist ambiguous data.

- **T8 hand-waves parsing.** “Parse names unquoted” is not a specification. Stripping display quotes will mishandle escapes, backslashes, embedded quotes, and delimiter collisions. The plan needs a machine-readable or explicitly framed template format compatible with the minimum supported jj version.

- **T3 may leave jj inconsistent.** Running `git rebase --abort` in a colocated repository can change Git refs/index without refreshing jj’s imported view. The plan must establish whether a subsequent `jj git import` or snapshot is required and ensure the command actually invokes Git rather than falling through a vcs-selected jj path.

- **T6 has no defined signal semantics.** `SIGTERM` from an intentional Stop, timeout escalation, external kill, and crash are not the same outcome. # v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md

## Context

Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.

What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.

No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.

## Landing shape

10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).

## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)

1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
   data-loss race.
   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
   **Fix decision:** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait` — this codebase already solved the
   identical gap for `commit` (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) not by
   raising the ceiling but by suppressing conflicting read lanes via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (checked by `isCommitting`/
   `isCommittingProject`) while a commit is in flight — the code's own comment explains why:
   "raising the ceiling would only make every other lane wait longer" (line 662), since a
   higher ceiling serializes *every* status probe on the project, not just the ones actually
   racing a live write. No equivalent `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` exists (grepped,
   confirmed absent). Mirror the commit pattern: add `fetchingProjectRoots`/
   `pullingProjectRoots` counters plus `isFetchingProject`/`isPullingProject` predicates, and
   wire them into the same read-lane guards `isCommittingProject` already gates (status
   sweep, file watcher, selection refresh).

## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix

3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.

4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` for a "cwd vanished" launch failure, and
   `classify` maps that to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git
   is fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

## Tier 3 — jj-shaped correctness bugs (included per broader-cut decision)

7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Real fix is remembering each
   workroom's own base rather than deriving it from `::@ & remote_bookmarks()`. Lives in
   `VCSWriting.swift` (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.

8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name. Parse
   names unquoted; build rebase destinations with `jjQuote` per-name rather than reusing a
   pre-joined display string.

9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.

## Also worth a look while touching this area

10. **CMT-3 — terminal content accessibility (minimal-viable only).** The only item whose
    own priority line explicitly says "address before GA." Two traps already resolved in
    TODOS.md so don't re-derive them: it is **not** blocked by the libghostty pin bump (one
    self-posted `.selectedTextChanged` notification is the whole cost on the currently pinned
    engine); and the target is deliberately minimal — `accessibilityValue()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `accessibilitySelectedText()` via
    `ghostty_surface_read_selection`, throttled `.valueChanged` + `.selectedTextChanged`
    posts. Explicitly skip the full `NSAccessibility` text-range/geometry protocol — overkill
    for a terminal, per the entry's own note (crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`).

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- **`GitHubAuthCache`** (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`, 114 lines) — the freshness-lease +
  generation-stamped in-flight + instance-ownership shape item #5 lifts wholesale, including
  its exact TTL numbers.
- **`committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`**
  (`AppStore.swift:333-341`, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:655-677`) — the read-lane
  suppression pattern item #2's fetch/pull fix mirrors exactly.
- **`Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`** (`VCSWriting.swift:1090,1323`)
  — the colocated-rebase detection item #3 reuses instead of writing new branching logic.
- **`CommandResult.signaled`** (shipped, gh-flap fix) — item #6 wires three more consumers
  into a mechanism that already exists and is tested; it does not add a new one.

## NOT in scope (considered, explicitly deferred)

- **libghostty pin bump, own-the-xcframework** — scheduled by TODOS.md for after the GA tag.
- **`withTimeout` caller-cancellation gap** — broad blast radius across every caller, "no
  user-visible bug today" per its own entry; wrong trade immediately before a landing push.
- **Native `theme = dark:X,light:Y` syntax** — zero user-visible gain, needs live-engine
  verification first; pure regression risk.
- **Search-counter UI test coverage** — its value is as the pin bump's tripwire; schedule
  with that post-GA work.
- **Deterministic tab lookup, git diff both-staged-and-modified** — no confirmed user impact
  worth the churn right now.
- **Everything filed as new capability** — VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch,
  structured diff hunks, notification prefs/persistence, PR review-status UI, theme content,
  OSC 99/auto-notify (blocked upstream), memory diagnostics tooling, quick-switcher
  deferrals, activity-bar search. Roadmap items, not bugs in what's shipped.
- **Report the gstack codex fix upstream** — not a workroom product item; out of scope
  regardless of cut depth.
- **A fourth `signaled` consumer in `VCSWriting.swift`** — checked, already fixed (see item
  #6's note); correctly excluded from that item's scope, not silently missed.
- **Hand-rolled PID-liveness locking (Go)** — considered as the fix for item #1, rejected in
  favor of an OS-level advisory-lock library; see item #1's fix decision.
- **Raising `JJSnapshotGate.defaultMaxChainWait`** — considered as the fix for item #2,
  rejected because it would slow every unrelated status probe on the project, not just the
  ones racing a live write; see item #2's fix decision.

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Lane A (Go, independent): #1. Lane B (VCSWriting.swift, sequential): #3 -> #7 -> #8 -> #9 —
all four touch the same file. Lane C (independent Core files, parallel-safe): #2, #4, #5,
#6 — four different files with no shared state. Lane D (independent subsystem): #10.

## Implementation Tasks (T1-T10)

T1 (P1): CLI, replace config lock with gofrs/flock. T2 (P1): macapp, add
isFetchingProject/isPullingProject mirroring isCommitting. T3 (P2): macapp, fix abortRebase
jj branch to check rebaseInProgress. T4 (P2): macapp, give cwd-vanished launch failure its
own sentinel. T5 (P2): macapp, lift GitHubAuthCache shape into VCSToolVersionCache. T6 (P2):
macapp, consume CommandResult.signaled in 3 remaining call sites. T7 (P2): macapp, remember
each workroom's own pull base instead of trunk(). T8 (P2): macapp, parse jj bookmark names
unquoted before comparing. T9 (P2): macapp, filter trackingByName by primaryRemote. T10
(P1): macapp, minimal-viable terminal content a11y (CMT-3).

- **T5’s proposed cache architecture does not solve the cited race.** A generation-stamped slot still permits a `probeJJ: false` result to replace a jj-aware aggregate verdict unless results are keyed or Git and jj are cached independently. “Instance ownership” may also create inconsistent verdicts and duplicate probes across consumers.

- **T4 assumes an error distinction the process API may not provide.** Spawn commonly reports `ENOENT` for both a missing executable and a missing working directory. A new enum case is useless without resolving the executable first or performing an explicit cwd check; the latter remains racy.

- **T7–T9 are one upstream-identity problem, not three independent patches.** Filtering `trackingByName` does not fix revsets still using `trunk()`, whose configured target may be another remote. Define one structured `(bookmark, remote, target commit)` model and use it for counts, labels, fetch, and rebase.

- **The jj sequencing is backwards.** Safe raw-name representation and revset quoting are prerequisites for storing or selecting a base. Implementing T7 before T8/T9 invites immediate rework and can persist ambiguous data.

- **T8 hand-waves parsing.** “Parse names unquoted” is not a specification. Stripping display quotes will mishandle escapes, backslashes, embedded quotes, and delimiter collisions. The plan needs a machine-readable or explicitly framed template format compatible with the minimum supported jj version.

- **T3 may leave jj inconsistent.** Running `git rebase --abort` in a colocated repository can change Git refs/index without refreshing jj’s imported view. The plan must establish whether a subsequent `jj git import` or snapshot is required and ensure the command actually invokes Git rather than falling through a vcs-selected jj path.

- **T6 has no defined signal semantics.** `SIGTERM` from an intentional Stop, timeout escalation, external kill, and crash are not the same outcome. Merely branching on `signaled` can replace “exit 9” with a different wrong claim. `FileTreeModel` also needs an error propagation design; a one-line branch cannot fix silent emptiness if its API only returns a list.

- **T10 may not provide usable accessibility.** Exposing the entire terminal as one changing string can be expensive and nearly unnavigable in VoiceOver. The plan omits accessibility role/element behavior, engine thread affinity, text-size limits, secure-content handling, and an actual VoiceOver acceptance test.

- **The claimed landing shape is internally inconsistent.** Tier 1 combines unrelated Go and Swift failures; Tier 2 combines four unrelated subsystems. Those PRs are not independently revertible or easy to bisect. Group by fix, not severity.

- **The file count and parallel-safety claims are unrealistic.** T2 already spans multiple store files; T4 touches runner and classification; T5 requires ownership/call-site changes; T7 implies persistence and migration. Several lanes will also collide in `VCSWriting.swift` and shared tests.

- **There is no release-quality verification plan.** The risky items need deterministic process-level lock tests, mixed old/new lock tests, gate tests exceeding 30 seconds, multiple-store write tests, jj fixtures covering quoted names and multiple remotes, cache concurrency tests, and VoiceOver/manual accessibility criteria. “A test each” for T6 is not enough.

- **The scope is strategically too large for a bugs-only GA pass.** T7 and T10 are underspecified feature-scale work, while T2’s proposed fix misses the corruption path. Fix the gate correctly, make locking rollout-safe, close the false-success/error-classification bugs, and defer anything requiring a new persistence or accessibility model.

191	/// `git --version` at launch. Concurrent callers share one probe rather than racing two.
192	///
193	/// `probedJJ` is remembered: a first probe taken before any jj project was registered legitimately
194	/// skipped `jj`, and reporting that cached `.notInstalled` once a jj project appears would warn about
195	/// a tool nobody ever looked for. Needing jj after skipping it re-probes.
196	actor VCSToolVersionCache {
197	  static let shared = VCSToolVersionCache()
198	
199	  private var cached: (report: VCSToolVersions.Report, probedJJ: Bool)?
200	  private var inFlight: (task: Task<VCSToolVersions.Report, Never>, probedJJ: Bool)?
201	
202	  func report(probeJJ: Bool, runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner()) async
203	    -> VCSToolVersions.Report
204	  {
205	    // Reuse only a result that covers what this caller needs.
206	    if let cached, cached.probedJJ || !probeJJ { return cached.report }
207	    if let inFlight, inFlight.probedJJ || !probeJJ { return await inFlight.task.value }
208	    let task = Task { await VCSToolVersions.probe(runner: runner, probeJJ: probeJJ) }
209	    inFlight = (task, probeJJ)
210	    let report = await task.value
211	    // Never cache a `.notInstalled`. That verdict comes from exit 127, i.e. the tool wasn't on PATH —
212	    // and at launch the PATH may still be the deterministic floor, because `ShellEnvironment.path()`
213	    // silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe lands and nothing joins that probe
214	    // (it is fired detached in `WorkroomApp.init`, while `refreshVCSToolReport` runs from
215	    // `apply(projects)`). The floor covers Homebrew but NOT a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or
216	    // MacPorts, so a jj living in one of those reads as missing — and caching that pinned "jj isn't
217	    // installed" for the entire process, since `cached` is only cleared by the tests-only `reset()`.
218	    // Re-probing costs one `--version` and by then the enriched PATH has usually landed.
219	    //
220	    // `.unknown` is safe to cache by contrast: `warnings(hasJJProject:)` ignores it, so it never
221	    // becomes a false claim.
222	    if !report.hasMissingTool(probedJJ: probeJJ) { cached = (report, probeJJ) }
223	    inFlight = nil
224	    return report
225	  }
226	
227	  /// Tests only — the cache is process-wide, so a test that probed must clear it.
228	  func reset() {
229	    cached = nil
230	    inFlight = nil
231	  }
232	}

content.text: The outside-voice pass came back sharp — three of its findings survive my own code verification and actually overturn or refine decisions I locked in earlier. Walking through them one at a time.

questions.question:
CROSS-MODEL TENSION 1 (confirmed real via my own code trace, confidence 9/10) — the earlier decision for item #2 doesn't actually close the bug TODOS.md describes.

The outside voice (Codex) flagged: "Read-lane suppression cannot stop a second fetch/pull from timing out after 30 seconds and entering concurrently." I verified this against the code: every existing isCommitting/isCommittingProject call site (AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:73,142,729) is in a READ path (status sweep, file watcher) — none of them gate a WRITE from starting. So mirroring that pattern for fetch/pull would stop background status reads from racing a live fetch/pull (a real improvement, matching what commit already gets) — but TODOS.md's item #9(9) describes two WRITES racing each other ("two windows... queue two writes... the second runs concurrently with a live pull --rebase"), and nothing I can find gates a second write from entering JJSnapshotGate's queue while a first is still running. The commit path has this SAME unaddressed exposure today (unverified whether anyone's hit it in practice — commits are usually fast; fetch/pull's 120-300s budgets make it routine). My earlier recommendation (mirror isCommitting) only fixes the read-vs-write half.

options.label: Extend the fix: gate writes too (recommended)
options.description: Add write-vs-write suppression alongside the read-lane suppression: before a fetch/pull/commit starts, check whether ANOTHER write is already in flight for that project and either queue behind it properly (wait the FULL duration, not capped at 30s) or surface a clear "already syncing" state instead of racing. This is the fix that actually closes the bug as described, but it's a real design decision (does JJSnapshotGate need a per-call maxWait, or does the write path need its own in-flight tracking like isCommittingProject but consulted by WRITES not just reads?) — needs its own sub-decision. Effort: human ~4-6h / CC ~40min (larger than originally scoped).

questions.question:
D-continuation: which shape for the write-vs-write fix itself?

Reasoning through the two candidates I offered: Option A (per-call maxWait on the gate) would make a queued write wait up to its own budget (120-300s) for a wedged predecessor before self-healing — correct, but weakens wedge-detection latency from 30s to 300s worst-case, and still lets two writes queue silently with no user-visible signal. Option B as drafted still allowed silent queueing too. A third shape falls out of extending the EXISTING committingTargets/committingProjectRoots pattern properly: have fetch/push/pull/commit check "is any write already in flight for this project" (a unified per-project write-in-flight flag, checked by the ACTION ITSELF, not just read lanes) and refuse outright with a clear "already syncing" state rather than queueing at all. No change to JJSnapshotGate's core self-heal semantics (the wedge-detection ceiling stays untouched, since that's a separate concern), and it matches how the toolbar already presents a single action per window — cross-window contention becomes an honest "try again" instead of a silent race.

Before starting any of them, check if another write is already in flight for the project; if so, refuse with a clear toast ("Already syncing this project in another window") instead of queueing. Simplest mechanism, no change to the gate's wedge-detection semantics, clearest UX. Effort: human ~3-4h / CC ~30min.

Reads keep the short default. Preserves today's "it just works, eventually" feel (no refusal message) but weakens wedge-detection to the write's full timeout, and a queued second write still isn't visible to the user while waiting.

questions.question:
CROSS-MODEL TENSION 4 (rollout-compatibility concern, plausible but lower urgency — confidence 6/10, not independently verified since it depends on real-world install-age distribution).

The outside voice flagged: "An older CLI can see the new process's lockfile, declare it stale after ten seconds, unlink it, and create a new inode. The old and new processes then hold unrelated locks." This is real for ANY change to the locking primitive: a NEW binary (macOS app's bundled CLI, or an updated standalone CLI) using a real OS advisory lock (flock) and an OLD, not-yet-updated standalone CLI still doing the current O_CREATE|O_EXCL scheme would use mechanisms that don't recognize each other at all — during that mixed-version window, the fix provides no MORE protection for that specific pairing than today's status quo (it's not a regression, but it's not the full fix either, for as long as an old CLI persists on a machine). Given no tag is being cut yet (nightly/dev only per your instruction), this window matters most at the eventual GA rollout, not right now.

options.label: Add a compatibility note now, decide the mechanism closer to the tag (recommended)
options.description: Record the risk in the plan as a rollout caveat for whoever cuts the eventual GA tag (e.g. "keep writing the legacy .lock sidecar file alongside the new flock for one release cycle, so an old un-upgraded CLI binary still sees SOME signal") without designing the exact compatibility shim now — the auto-updater's cadence and how many users run a detached standalone CLI vs. the bundled one matters for how real this risk is in practice, and that's better assessed near the actual tag than speculated now.
options.preview:

More upfront design work for a rollout concern that's a release-time decision, not a dev/nightly one.

input.old_string:
**Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
   precedent in this codebase to lean on.

input.new_string:
**Fix decision (revised after outside-voice review):** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait`
   — this codebase already solved the analogous READ-vs-WRITE half of this gap for `commit`
   (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) via
   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`)
   suppressing conflicting read lanes while a commit is in flight. Mirroring that pattern for
   fetch/pull alone was the original plan here — **but verification during review showed
   every existing call site of that mechanism (lines 73, 142, 729) is a READ path; nothing
   gates a second WRITE from starting.** TODOS.md's item describes two WRITES racing each
   other, which the read-lane mirror does not close (the commit path has this same
   unaddressed exposure today). **Revised fix:** extend the tracking to a unified
   per-project write-in-flight concept covering fetch/push/pull/commit together, and have
   the write ACTIONS THEMSELVES (not just read lanes) check it before starting — refusing
   outright with a clear "already syncing this project in another window" message rather
   than queuing into the gate and possibly racing. This leaves `JJSnapshotGate`'s own
   wedge-detection ceiling (30s) untouched — that's a separate, correct mechanism for a
   genuinely-hung call — and gives cross-window contention an honest, visible outcome
   instead of a silent race or a long silent wait.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Lift the `GitHubAuthCache` shape (`Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`)
   wholesale into `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight
   slot, instance ownership instead of `static let shared`. Also closes a real reentrancy bug
   where a `probeJJ: false` caller can overwrite a concurrent jj-aware verdict.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) rather than inventing new numbers. A tool's
   installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of re-probing
   every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer, bespoke TTL
   isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
   until they relaunch the app. Also closes a real reentrancy bug, traced exactly at
   `VCSToolVersions.swift:202-224`: caller B (`probeJJ: false`) starts first and becomes
   `inFlight`; caller A (`probeJJ: true`) arrives while B runs, doesn't reuse B's inFlight
   (wrong coverage), and overwrites the shared `inFlight` slot with its own task — B's own
   task keeps running independently, but whichever of A/B's completion runs LAST
   unconditionally overwrites `cached`. If B (jj-blind) finishes after A (jj-aware), B's
   report clobbers A's.
   **Architecture decision (revised after outside-voice review):** the original plan said
   "lift `GitHubAuthCache`'s shape wholesale" — but `GitHubAuthCache` has no `probeJJ`-style
   coverage axis at all, so a naive transplant only imports TEMPORAL generation-stamping and
   does not structurally prevent a less-informative probe from overwriting a more-informative
   one. **Revised fix:** split into two independent cache slots — a git slot and a jj slot,
   each an exact `GitHubAuthCache`-shaped instance (its own TTL, generation-stamped in-flight,
   instance ownership) — instead of one combined `Report` with a `probedJJ` side-flag. This
   eliminates the whole "wrong probe overwrites right probe" class structurally: there's no
   shared slot left for two different-coverage probes to race over, since git callers only
   ever touch the git slot and jj callers only ever touch the jj slot.
   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) for BOTH slots, rather than inventing new numbers.
   A tool's installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of
   re-probing every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer,
   bespoke TTL isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.

## Outside voice (Codex) — cross-model tensions and resolutions

Codex reviewed this plan independently (its own sandbox blocked repo reads, so its findings
were plan-text-only reasoning — each was verified against the actual source before being
accepted or rejected below). Four tensions survived verification and changed the plan;
several others were checked and found not applicable.

**Accepted, changed the plan:**
1. **Item #2's original fix (mirror `isCommitting` for fetch/pull) only closes read-vs-write
   contention, not the write-vs-write race TODOS.md actually describes.** Verified: every
   existing `isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject` call site is a read path; nothing gates a
   second write from starting. Revised to a unified write-in-flight flag that write actions
   check themselves, refusing outright rather than queuing.
2. **Item #5's "lift `GitHubAuthCache` wholesale" doesn't structurally prevent a jj-blind
   probe from clobbering a jj-aware cached verdict**, since `GitHubAuthCache` has no
   coverage axis to protect. Verified by tracing the actual reentrancy bug in
   `VCSToolVersions.swift:202-224`. Revised to two independent cache slots.
3. **Item #7's "remember each workroom's own base" is feature-scale work** (persistence,
   migration, staleness handling), not bug-fix-scoped for a "bugs and polish only" GA pass.
   Revised to report "no known upstream" and disable Pull instead.
4. **Item #1's OS-level lock has a mixed-version rollout gap** with an old, un-upgraded
   standalone CLI. Added as an explicit caveat for whoever cuts the eventual GA tag — not a
   decision for this dev/nightly pass.

**Accepted, added as implementation notes (no plan-shape change):**
- Item #3: verify whether a `jj git import` is needed after a real `git rebase --abort` in
  a colocated root.
- Item #4: the distinguishing info for cwd-vanished vs. tool-missing already exists in the
  caught error's captured `stderr` text — match on it rather than needing a new check.
- Item #8: "parse unquoted" needed an exact spec — `jjUnquote` as `jjQuote`'s literal
  inverse, not a naive strip.
- Item #10: don't expose content a terminal would normally mask (e.g. password prompts)
  through the new accessibility value.

**Checked and found not applicable:**
- "Advisory locking prevents nothing if any writer bypasses `withLock`" — verified every
  config mutator (`AddWorkroom`, `AddProject`, etc.) already reads and writes inside the
  same `withLock` closure, and `Config.Write` has no external callers. No bypass exists.
- "`FileTreeModel` needs an error-propagation design, not just a branch" and "T6 has no
  defined signal semantics" — item #6's actual scope (per TODOS.md and the already-shipped
  precedent at `VCSWriting.swift:1108`) is narrower than Codex assumed: report "interrupted,"
  not differentiate signal causes. Matches an existing, shipped pattern; no change needed.
- "T10 may not provide usable accessibility" (thread affinity, size limits, navigability) —
  TODOS.md's own CMT-3 entry already scopes this explicitly ("announce output + selection,
  navigable text, not a perfect document model") and rules out the concerns Codex raised
  (full text-range protocol). Already addressed by the entry's own stated scope.
- "The landing shape is internally inconsistent" (group by fix, not by tier) — the user
  already made this call explicitly (see Landing shape section) with clear reasoning
  (blast-radius grouping, matches this repo's changelog pattern); not re-litigated.
- "No release-quality verification plan" — Codex reviewed a trimmed prompt that excluded
  this plan's Test coverage diagram and Failure modes table; both already exist in the full
  plan with per-item test cases.

content.content:
1	# v2 GA bug/polish scope — what to pull from TODOS.md
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Workroom v2 is about to ship as GA (final). The mandate from here is bugs and polish only —
6	no new features, no roadmap items. `TODOS.md` has 61 open/closed entries spanning P1–P3, but
7	most of them are either already-shipped changelog noise, deliberately-deferred features
8	(VCS write Phase 2, new-workroom-from-branch, notification prefs, PR-review UI, theme
9	content, diagnostics tooling), or infra work the file itself schedules for *after* the GA
10	tag (the libghostty pin bump, owning the GhosttyKit xcframework). None of those belong here.
11	
12	What's left, sorted by "does a user in a default config hit this, and does it produce a
13	wrong claim, silent data loss, or an inescapable dead end" — the right discriminator for a
14	GA push, not "is it labeled P1/P2/P3" (several real bugs are filed P3, several inert items
15	are filed P2) — is the list below. Scope decision from the user: **broader cut** — include
16	the jj-shaped VCS-toolbar correctness bugs (Tier 3) alongside the silent-damage and
17	wrong-claim items (Tiers 1–2), not just the tightest possible cut.
18	
19	No tag is being cut right now — this work targets `master`/dev and rides the daily nightly
20	build, per the user's explicit instruction. That said, two release-mechanics facts are worth
21	flagging now (as checks to do *when* a GA tag is actually imminent, not as work items for
22	this pass): v2.0.0 will be the first **stable** tag after a long prerelease run, so the
23	three lockstepped channel-classification implementations (`internal/channel`,
24	`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift`, `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh`) need to
25	agree a `v2.0.0` tag is `stable`; and the arm64-only-CLI fix (`build-helper.sh` per-arch
26	build + `lipo`, `release.sh check_universal()`) is already fixed in tree per TODOS.md but
27	unreleased, so it will ship automatically once nightly/the eventual tag builds off master —
28	nothing to do for it beyond letting it ride.
29	
30	## Landing shape
31	
32	10 independent bug items span ~8-10 files across unrelated subsystems (CLI config locking,
33	Swift VCS gate timing, tool-version caching, process signal handling, jj bookmark parsing,
34	terminal accessibility). Per-item risk is low, but one combined diff would make review and
35	bisection harder if any single item regressed. Decision: land as **4 PRs, grouped by tier**
36	— Tier 1 (config lock + JJSnapshotGate), Tier 2 (colocated-jj abort + PATH sentinel + stale
37	version cache + signaled consumers), Tier 3 (jj Pull base + bookmark quoting + multi-remote
38	tracking, jj-only), and CMT-3 standalone (different subsystem, different risk profile,
39	accessibility-only). This groups by blast radius/subsystem, keeps each PR independently
40	revertible, and matches this repo's own changelog pattern of small dated commits (see
41	TODOS.md's "Recently done" section).
42	
43	## Tier 1 — silent damage (highest priority)
44	
45	1. **Config lock can be stolen from a live holder (CLI).** Verified at
46	   `internal/config/config.go:120-145`: `withLock` hand-rolls locking via
47	   `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` plus a stale-file mtime check
48	   (`time.Since(info.ModTime()) > 10*time.Second` at line 137) — a busy-wait polling scheme,
49	   not real OS-level locking, so "stale" is measured by elapsed time, never by whether the
50	   holder is actually alive. Two concurrent writers can silently clobber each other's config
51	   edit — a workroom or project can vanish from the sidebar with no error shown. This is in
52	   the engine both the CLI and the macOS app drive, so it's the highest-leverage fix in the
53	   list. TODOS.md files this P3 ("cheap to close") — the label undersells it; it's a real
54	   data-loss race.
55	   **Fix decision:** replace the hand-rolled scheme with a real OS-level advisory lock via a
56	   small, well-established library (e.g. `github.com/gofrs/flock`, wrapping `flock(2)` on
57	   Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows) rather than adding hand-written PID-liveness checking.
58	   No such locking dependency exists anywhere in this Go codebase today (grepped, confirmed
59	   absent), so this is new territory either way — the library path gets liveness for free
60	   (the OS releases the lock when the holding process dies or crashes, no stale-timeout
61	   heuristic to tune at all), where a hand-rolled PID check would need separate,
62	   easy-to-get-wrong Unix (`signal 0`) and Windows (`OpenProcess`) implementations with no
63	   precedent in this codebase to lean on.
64	   **Rollout caveat (outside-voice tension, resolved):** an old, un-upgraded standalone CLI
65	   binary still doing the current `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` + mtime scheme and a new flock-based
66	   binary don't recognize each other's lock at all — during that mixed-version window this
67	   fix is no worse than today's status quo for that specific pairing, but it isn't the full
68	   fix either. Not a decision for this pass (no tag is being cut right now) — **whoever cuts
69	   the eventual GA tag must decide** whether the new `withLock` should also touch the legacy
70	   `.lock` sidecar file for one release cycle, so an old CLI's staleness heuristic at least
71	   sees a fresh mtime from a live new-style holder instead of misreading it as abandoned.
72	
73	2. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** Fetch is
74	   budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so the gate re-admitting a chain past 30s is *routine*
75	   contention, not the rare wedge case it's justified as. Two windows/AppStores can each
76	   queue a write on the same project root; the second gives up its wait and runs concurrently
77	   with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`. This is the scariest unfixed VCS item —
78	   real corruption risk under ordinary multi-window use, not an edge case.
79	   **Fix decision (revised after outside-voice review):** do NOT raise `defaultMaxChainWait`
80	   — this codebase already solved the analogous READ-vs-WRITE half of this gap for `commit`
81	   (verified at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:658-677`) via
82	   `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots` (`isCommitting`/`isCommittingProject`)
83	   suppressing conflicting read lanes while a commit is in flight. Mirroring that pattern for
84	   fetch/pull alone was the original plan here — **but verification during review showed
85	   every existing call site of that mechanism (lines 73, 142, 729) is a READ path; nothing
86	   gates a second WRITE from starting.** TODOS.md's item describes two WRITES racing each
87	   other, which the read-lane mirror does not close (the commit path has this same
88	   unaddressed exposure today). **Revised fix:** extend the tracking to a unified
89	   per-project write-in-flight concept covering fetch/push/pull/commit together, and have
90	   the write ACTIONS THEMSELVES (not just read lanes) check it before starting — refusing
91	   outright with a clear "already syncing this project in another window" message rather
92	   than queuing into the gate and possibly racing. This leaves `JJSnapshotGate`'s own
93	   wedge-detection ceiling (30s) untouched — that's a separate, correct mechanism for a
94	   genuinely-hung call — and gives cross-window contention an honest, visible outcome
95	   instead of a silent race or a long silent wait.
96	
97	## Tier 2 — wrong claim shown to the user, cheap to fix
98	
99	3. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** Verified
100	   at `VCSWriting.swift:1618-1622`: `abortRebase`'s jj branch is
101	   `guard vcs != "jj" else { return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort") }` — it returns fake
102	   success unconditionally for ANY jj repo, without checking disk state at all, before ever
103	   looking at whether a colocated `.git` actually has a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase`
104	   run in the terminal. `classify` can hand such a colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` (via
105	   the same file's `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` check at line 1090), so the failure clears
106	   without fixing anything, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns. Inescapable
107	   in-app without knowing to drop to a terminal.
108	   **Fix decision:** reuse `Self.worktreeGitDir(at:)` + the existing `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)`
109	   helper (already used identically at line 1090 for pull's classify path) — only return
110	   "Nothing to abort" when that check finds no real git-side rebase state; otherwise fall
111	   through to the actual git abort-rebase command against that `gitDir`. Reuses existing
112	   detection rather than inventing separate colocated-vs-not branching logic.
113	   **Verify during implementation (outside-voice note, not yet resolved):** confirm whether
114	   running the real `git rebase --abort` against a colocated root's `.git` needs a follow-up
115	   `jj git import`/snapshot for jj's own view to reflect the reverted refs, or whether jj's
116	   next status read (which already re-snapshots `@` on every read) naturally picks it up. If
117	   the toolbar's existing post-action status refresh doesn't show the corrected state, add
118	   the explicit import as part of this fix rather than shipping a fix that still looks stale.

120	4. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH."**
121	   `StatusCommandRunner` returns `commandNotFound` (exit 127) for BOTH a real missing-tool
122	   case and a "cwd vanished" launch failure (verified at `StatusCommandRunner.swift:319-330`
123	   — `catch { ... exitCode: CommandResult.commandNotFound }`), and `classify` maps that
124	   single sentinel to `.toolMissing` — while the version toast simultaneously says git is
125	   fine. Needs its own launch-failure sentinel distinct from tool-missing.
126	   **Implementation note:** the catch site already preserves the real cause —
127	   `stderr: "\(error)"` captures the caught `Process.run()` error's full description, which
128	   differs between "executable not found" and "working directory doesn't exist." The fix
129	   should pattern-match that captured text (same technique the git/jj classifiers already
130	   use for lock detection elsewhere in this file) rather than needing a new syscall-level
131	   check — the distinguishing information already exists, it's just discarded downstream at
132	   classification time today.
133	
134	5. **`VCSToolVersionCache` pins a stale tool verdict for the whole process.**
135	   `.belowFloor` (and everything except `.notInstalled`) is cached forever — a user reads
136	   "Git 2.41 or newer required," runs `brew upgrade git`, and fetch/push/pull stay disabled
137	   until they relaunch the app. Also closes a real reentrancy bug, traced exactly at
138	   `VCSToolVersions.swift:202-224`: caller B (`probeJJ: false`) starts first and becomes
139	   `inFlight`; caller A (`probeJJ: true`) arrives while B runs, doesn't reuse B's inFlight
140	   (wrong coverage), and overwrites the shared `inFlight` slot with its own task — B's own
141	   task keeps running independently, but whichever of A/B's completion runs LAST
142	   unconditionally overwrites `cached`. If B (jj-blind) finishes after A (jj-aware), B's
143	   report clobbers A's.
144	   **Architecture decision (revised after outside-voice review):** the original plan said
145	   "lift `GitHubAuthCache`'s shape wholesale" — but `GitHubAuthCache` has no `probeJJ`-style
146	   coverage axis at all, so a naive transplant only imports TEMPORAL generation-stamping and
147	   does not structurally prevent a less-informative probe from overwriting a more-informative
148	   one. **Revised fix:** split into two independent cache slots — a git slot and a jj slot,
149	   each an exact `GitHubAuthCache`-shaped instance (its own TTL, generation-stamped in-flight,
150	   instance ownership) — instead of one combined `Report` with a `probedJJ` side-flag. This
151	   eliminates the whole "wrong probe overwrites right probe" class structurally: there's no
152	   shared slot left for two different-coverage probes to race over, since git callers only
153	   ever touch the git slot and jj callers only ever touch the jj slot.
154	   **TTL decision:** reuse `GitHubAuthCache`'s exact values (60s positive / 10s negative —
155	   verified at `GitHubAuthCache.swift:60`) for BOTH slots, rather than inventing new numbers.
156	   A tool's installed version changes far less than GitHub auth state, but the cost of
157	   re-probing every 60s (one local `--version` subprocess) is cheap enough that a longer,
158	   bespoke TTL isn't worth the extra tuning surface and its own test cases.
159	
160	6. **`CommandResult.signaled` isn't consumed by three call sites.** Verified: `AgentRunner`
161	   `.swift:177` (`if result.exitCode != 0 { ... return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, ...) }`,
162	   no `signaled` check before this branch), `FileTreeModel.swift:150`
163	   (`if result.ok { return FileListing.parse(...) }` — a signalled listing renders as a
164	   silently empty file tree), and `RustJJProvider.swift:237-238`
165	   (`guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode)...") }`)
166	   all still read a killed child's signal number as a real exit code. User-visible: a killed
167	   `claude` agent shows "exit 9" in the banner — exactly the nonsense class the original
168	   gh-flap fix was meant to end. One-line branch per site (mind `timedOut` implies
169	   `signaled`, so check order matters in `AgentRunner.classify`) plus a test each; the
170	   mechanism (`CommandResult.signaled`) is already shipped and tested. Note: a fourth
171	   candidate site, `VCSWriting.swift`'s git-error classifier, was checked and is **already
172	   fixed** (`VCSWriting.swift:1108`: `if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other(...) }`)
173	   — do not re-touch it, it's not part of this item's scope.

177	7. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Wrong for a workroom
178	   off a feature branch: reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits, then the rebase refuses
179	   (typed, retry-free — fails honestly, but still wrong). Lives in `VCSWriting.swift`
180	   (`CLIVCSWriter`), same file as items #3 and #9.
181	   **Scope decision (revised after outside-voice review):** TODOS.md's original framing
182	   ("remembering each workroom's own base") implies new persistent state — a config field,
183	   a migration path for every workroom created before this fix ships, and undefined behavior
184	   for what happens when the remembered base is later renamed/deleted/force-pushed. That's
185	   feature-scale work, not a bug fix, and cuts against this pass's own "bugs and polish
186	   only" mandate. **Revised, GA-appropriate fix:** for an unbookmarked `@` off a non-trunk
187	   base, stop guessing `trunk()` as the comparison point — report "no known upstream" and
188	   disable the Pull action (with a tooltip explaining why) instead of computing a wrong
189	   "N behind" and then failing the rebase. Ships the honest half (stop lying about the
190	   count) without committing to the unspecified feature (remembering a base) TODOS.md never
191	   fully designed.
192	
193	8. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** Verified at `VCSWriting.swift:1442`:
194	   `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }` — jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier
195	   names (e.g. `"main|evil"`), so comparing against jj-lib's raw unquoted name always fails —
196	   tracking, counts, and Pull go silently nil for anyone using such a bookmark name.
197	   **Implementation note (outside-voice: "parse unquoted" was underspecified):** `jjQuote`
198	   already exists (`VCSWriting.swift:755-759`) and escapes `\` → `\\` then `"` → `\"` before
199	   wrapping in `"..."`. The fix needs a `jjUnquote` that is the exact inverse — strip
200	   surrounding quotes if present, then reverse the escaping in the same order jjQuote applies
201	   it (`\\"` → `"`, `\\\\` → `\`) — not a naive strip of the first/last character, which
202	   would mishandle a name containing an escaped quote or backslash. Build rebase
203	   destinations with `jjQuote` per-name (already correct in the original plan) rather than
204	   reusing a pre-joined display string.
205	
206	9. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** Verified at
207	   `VCSWriting.swift:983-1005`: `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by name with no
208	   `primaryRemote` filter — with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main`, the last row
209	   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. Same root
210	   cause lets `@..trunk()` count against a different remote than the one named/fetched.
