1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"sync"
5		"testing"
6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/gofrs/flock"
9	)
10	
11	// TestWithLockSerializesAgainstALiveSlowHolder proves the bug this fix closes:
12	// a holder that is merely slow (not crashed) must never have its lock stolen,
13	// and the two writers' fn calls must never run concurrently. The old
14	// mtime-staleness scheme would misdiagnose a holder still working past 10s as
15	// abandoned; a real OS advisory lock never does, however long the holder runs.
16	func TestWithLockSerializesAgainstALiveSlowHolder(t *testing.T) {
17		c := newTestConfig(t)
18	
19		var mu sync.Mutex
20		inFlight := false
21		overlapped := false
22		var order []string
23	
24		holdFor := 150 * time.Millisecond
25	
26		run := func(name string, hold time.Duration) {
27			err := c.withLock(func() error {
28				mu.Lock()
29				if inFlight {
30					overlapped = true
31				}
32				inFlight = true
33				order = append(order, name+":start")
34				mu.Unlock()
35	
36				time.Sleep(hold)
37	
38				mu.Lock()
39				order = append(order, name+":end")
40				inFlight = false
41				mu.Unlock()
42				return nil
43			})
44			if err != nil {
45				t.Errorf("%s: withLock returned error: %v", name, err)
46			}
47		}
48	
49		var wg sync.WaitGroup
50		wg.Add(2)
51		go func() {
52			defer wg.Done()
53			run("A", holdFor)
54		}()
55		// Give A a head start so it reliably acquires the lock first.
56		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
57		go func() {
58			defer wg.Done()
59			run("B", 10*time.Millisecond)
60		}()
61		wg.Wait()
62	
63		if overlapped {
64			t.Fatalf("A and B's fn calls overlapped — lock did not serialize a live holder: %v", order)
65		}
66		if len(order) != 4 {
67			t.Fatalf("expected 4 ordered events, got %v", order)
68		}
69		// A must fully finish (start+end) before B starts, since A held the lock
70		// first and B must wait for the real holder rather than stealing it.
71		if !(order[0] == "A:start" && order[1] == "A:end" && order[2] == "B:start" && order[3] == "B:end") {
72			t.Fatalf("expected A to fully finish before B started, got %v", order)
73		}
74	}
75	
76	// TestWithLockConcurrentWritersNeverCorruptTheFile drives many concurrent
77	// AddWorkroom calls (real withLock-guarded mutators) and asserts every one of
78	// them lands in the final config — proving the lock actually prevents the
79	// lost-update race the old stale-timeout scheme allowed.
80	func TestWithLockConcurrentWritersNeverCorruptTheFile(t *testing.T) {
81		c := newTestConfig(t)
82	
83		const n = 20
84		var wg sync.WaitGroup
85		errs := make([]error, n)
86		for i := range n {
87			wg.Add(1)
88			go func(i int) {
89				defer wg.Done()
90				errs[i] = c.AddWorkroom("/proj", nameFor(i), pathFor(i), "git")
91			}(i)
92		}
93		wg.Wait()
94	
95		for i, err := range errs {
96			if err != nil {
97				t.Fatalf("AddWorkroom %d failed: %v", i, err)
98			}
99		}
100	
101		names, err := c.WorkroomNames("/proj")
102		if err != nil {
103			t.Fatal(err)
104		}
105		if len(names) != n {
106			t.Fatalf("expected %d workrooms, got %d: %v (lost-update corruption)", n, len(names), names)
107		}
108	}
109	
110	func nameFor(i int) string { return "wr" + string(rune('a'+i%26)) + string(rune('0'+i/26)) }
111	func pathFor(i int) string { return "/wr/" + nameFor(i) }
112	
113	// TestWithLockReleasedImmediatelyWhenHolderDies proves the property that makes
114	// the stale-timeout heuristic unnecessary: an OS advisory lock is released by
115	// the kernel the instant the holding file descriptor closes (simulating a
116	// crashed process), not after some elapsed-time guess. A fresh acquisition on
117	// the same path must succeed right away — no waiting for any staleness window.
118	func TestWithLockReleasedImmediatelyWhenHolderDies(t *testing.T) {
119		c := newTestConfig(t)
120		lockPath := c.Path() + ".lock"
121	
122		// Simulate another process holding the lock, then dying without a clean
123		// unlock — closing the fd is what a crash does; gofrs/flock's Close() is
124		// the OS-level equivalent (no explicit Unlock call).
125		crashed := flock.New(lockPath)
126		locked, err := crashed.TryLock()
127		if err != nil || !locked {
128			t.Fatalf("setup: could not take the simulated crashed holder's lock: locked=%v err=%v", locked, err)
129		}
130		if err := crashed.Close(); err != nil {
131			t.Fatalf("setup: closing the simulated crashed holder's fd: %v", err)
132		}
133	
134		// A fresh call must succeed immediately — no 10s (or any) staleness wait.
135		start := time.Now()
136		if err := c.withLock(func() error { return nil }); err != nil {
137			t.Fatalf("withLock after a crashed holder returned error: %v", err)
138		}
139		if elapsed := time.Since(start); elapsed > time.Second {
140			t.Fatalf("withLock took %v after a crashed holder — expected near-instant reacquisition", elapsed)
141		}
142	}

1	import XCTest
2	
3	@testable import Workroom
4	
5	/// `AppStore.isWritingProject`/`beginWrite`/`endWrite` — the cross-window write-in-flight refusal
6	/// (VCS-foundation eng-review). `committingProjectRoots`/`isCommittingProject` exist to suppress READ
7	/// lanes during a commit; this is the separate, umbrella mechanism that all four write kinds
8	/// (commit/fetch/push/pull) check BEFORE starting, so a second write on the same project root is
9	/// refused outright instead of queuing into `JJSnapshotGate` and possibly racing a live one past the
10	/// gate's own wedge-detection ceiling.
11	@MainActor
12	final class AppStoreWritingProjectTests: XCTestCase {
13	
14	  private func makeStore(_ projects: [Project]) -> AppStore {
15	    let store = AppStore()
16	    store.projects = projects
17	    return store
18	  }
19	
20	  private func project(_ path: String, workrooms: [String]) -> Project {
21	    Project(
22	      path: path, vcs: "git",
23	      workrooms: workrooms.map {
24	        Workroom(name: $0, path: "\(path)/\($0)", vcsName: "main", warnings: [])
25	      })
26	  }
27	
28	  func testIsWritingProjectTracksBeginAndEnd() {
29	    let store = makeStore([])
30	    XCTAssertFalse(store.isWritingProject("/proj"))
31	    store.beginWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
32	    XCTAssertTrue(store.isWritingProject("/proj"))
33	    store.endWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
34	    XCTAssertFalse(store.isWritingProject("/proj"))
35	  }
36	
37	  func testIsWritingProjectIsPerProjectRoot() {
38	    let store = makeStore([])
39	    store.beginWrite(projectRoot: "/a")
40	    XCTAssertTrue(store.isWritingProject("/a"))
41	    XCTAssertFalse(store.isWritingProject("/b"), "a different project root must be unaffected")
42	  }
43	
44	  /// Counted, not a flag: two sibling writes can legitimately be marked in flight against one root
45	  /// (defensive symmetry with `committingProjectRoots`, even though in steady state
46	  /// `isWritingProject` refuses a second write before a second `beginWrite` is ever reached).
47	  func testEndWriteDecrementsRatherThanClears() {
48	    let store = makeStore([])
49	    store.beginWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
50	    store.beginWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
51	    store.endWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
52	    XCTAssertTrue(
53	      store.isWritingProject("/proj"), "one of two writes finished — the other is still in flight")
54	    store.endWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
55	    XCTAssertFalse(store.isWritingProject("/proj"))
56	  }
57	
58	  /// `endWrite` on a root with no recorded write must not underflow into a negative count that
59	  /// would make `isWritingProject` report busy forever.
60	  func testEndWriteOnAnUntrackedRootIsSafe() {
61	    let store = makeStore([])
62	    store.endWrite(projectRoot: "/never-began")
63	    XCTAssertFalse(store.isWritingProject("/never-began"))
64	  }
65	
66	  /// `performCommit` must refuse immediately — never touching the writer, never entering
67	  /// `committingTargets` — when another write is already in flight for the same project root.
68	  func testPerformCommitRefusesWhenAnotherWriteIsInFlight() {
69	    let store = makeStore([project("/proj", workrooms: ["feat"])])
70	    let sid = SidebarID.workroom(project: "/proj", name: "feat")
71	    store.beginWrite(projectRoot: "/proj")
72	
73	    let request = VCSCommitRequest(message: "msg", files: [], mode: .commit)
74	    var results: [VCSCommitResult] = []
75	    store.performCommit(request, on: sid) { results.append($0) }
76	
77	    XCTAssertEqual(results, [.failed(.locked(nil))])
78	    XCTAssertFalse(
79	      store.isCommitting(sid), "the refused commit must never have marked itself as committing")
80	  }
81	
82	  /// The common case: no other write in flight, so `performCommit` must proceed past the guard (it
83	  /// marks `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`writingProjectRoots` synchronously before
84	  /// its `Task` even starts) rather than refusing.
85	  func testPerformCommitProceedsWhenNoOtherWriteIsInFlight() {
86	    let store = makeStore([project("/proj", workrooms: ["feat"])])
87	    let sid = SidebarID.workroom(project: "/proj", name: "feat")
88	
89	    let request = VCSCommitRequest(message: "msg", files: [], mode: .commit)
90	    store.performCommit(request, on: sid) { _ in }
91	
92	    XCTAssertTrue(store.isCommitting(sid), "a real attempt must mark itself as committing")
93	    XCTAssertTrue(store.isWritingProject("/proj"))
94	  }
95	}
96

- Input sanitization with no test for malicious input

1	# Performance Specialist Review Checklist
2	
3	Scope: When SCOPE_BACKEND=true OR SCOPE_FRONTEND=true
4	Output: JSON objects, one finding per line. Schema:
5	{"severity":"CRITICAL|INFORMATIONAL","confidence":N,"path":"file","line":N,"category":"performance","summary":"...","fix":"...","fingerprint":"path:line:performance","specialist":"performance"}
6	Optional: line, fix, fingerprint, evidence, test_stub.
7	If no findings: output `NO FINDINGS` and nothing else.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Categories
12	
13	### N+1 Queries
14	- ActiveRecord/ORM associations traversed in loops without eager loading (.includes, joinedload, include)
15	- Database queries inside iteration blocks (each, map, forEach) that could be batched
16	- Nested serializers that trigger lazy-loaded associations
17	- GraphQL resolvers that query per-field instead of batching (check for DataLoader usage)
18	
19	### Missing Database Indexes
20	- New WHERE clauses on columns without indexes (check migration files or schema)
21	- New ORDER BY on non-indexed columns
22	- Composite queries (WHERE a AND b) without composite indexes
23	- Foreign key columns added without indexes
24	
25	### Algorithmic Complexity
26	- O(n^2) or worse patterns: nested loops over collections, Array.find inside Array.map
27	- Repeated linear searches that could use a hash/map/set lookup
28	- String concatenation in loops (use join or StringBuilder)
29	- Sorting or filtering large collections multiple times when once would suffice
30	
31	### Bundle Size Impact (Frontend)
32	- New production dependencies that are known-heavy (moment.js, lodash full, jquery)
33	- Barrel imports (import from 'library') instead of deep imports (import from 'library/specific')
34	- Large static assets (images, fonts) committed without optimization
35	- Missing code splitting for route-level chunks
36	
37	### Rendering Performance (Frontend)
38	- Fetch waterfalls: sequential API calls that could be parallel (Promise.all)
39	- Unnecessary re-renders from unstable references (new objects/arrays in render)
40	- Missing React.memo, useMemo, or useCallback on expensive computations
41	- Layout thrashing from reading then writing DOM properties in loops
42	- Missing loading="lazy" on below-fold images
43	
44	### Missing Pagination
45	- List endpoints that return unbounded results (no LIMIT, no pagination params)
46	- Database queries without LIMIT that grow with data volume
47	- API responses that embed full nested objects instead of IDs with expansion
48	
49	### Blocking in Async Contexts
50	- Synchronous I/O (file reads, subprocess, HTTP requests) inside async functions
51	- time.sleep() / Thread.sleep() inside event-loop-based handlers
52	- CPU-intensive computation blocking the main thread without worker offload
53

- Repeated linear searches that could use a hash/map/set lookup
- String concatenation in loops (use join or StringBuilder)
- Sorting or filtering large collections multiple times when once would suffice

- Synchronous I/O (file reads, subprocess, HTTP requests) inside async functions

455	
456	### VCS toolbar: the findings the `/review` pass didn't fix (macapp)
457	
458	**What:** Everything the toolbar review verified but left standing. Each was reproduced or read off the
459	code; none is speculative. Ordered by what a user hits first.
460	
461	**Six have since SHIPPED and are struck below**, so the list is what remains:
462	
463	- **the empty-remote case** (was (1)): `CLIVCSWriter.mergeRemotes` now unions the configured remote list
464	  (`git remote`, `jj git remote list`) with the ref-derived names for both backends, so publishing to a
465	  brand-new empty remote works and the counts stay ref-derived.
466	- **(5), (6) and (7)** — the three a user noticed — see each entry.
467	
468	2. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Right for a workroom off trunk,
469	   wrong for one off a feature branch: it reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits and the rebase
470	   then refuses (`immutableHistory`, now typed and retry-free, so it fails honestly rather than looping).
471	   **Correction (2026-08-10): the "wrong for a feature branch" claim above does not reproduce.**
472	   Three ancestor-based revsets were tried against real jj repos while attempting a fix — `trunk() &
473	   ::@`, either-direction ancestry, and `(trunk()..@) & ::(immutable_heads())` — and all were falsified
474	   empirically; the last one was tested against a constructed feature-branch-with-independently-
475	   advancing-trunk scenario, and the real `jj rebase -b @ -d trunk()` command in that exact scenario
476	   **succeeded** (exit 0, "Rebased 2 commits to destination") rather than hitting
477	   `immutable_heads()`. jj's default `immutable_heads()` is `trunk()`-ancestors only — a merely-pushed
478	   feature bookmark isn't protected by it — which is likely why this entry's own measurement isn't
479	   reproducible from its stated recipe. Reopening this needs a fresh, documented repro (the exact repo
480	   shape and jj version that produced `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`), not another revset
481	   guess. The original "remember each workroom's own base" fix idea below is unaffected either way —
482	   it was already out of scope for a bug-fix pass (needs persistence + a migration path), independent
483	   of whether the triggering scenario reproduces.
484	   The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base rather than deriving it — `::@ &
485	   remote_bookmarks()` can't, because the base stops being an ancestor the moment it advances.
486	3. ~~**jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.**~~ **SHIPPED.** jj's template pre-quotes
487	   non-identifier names (verified: `"main|evil"` comes back WITH the quotes) — `jjUnquote` (the exact
488	   inverse of `jjQuote`) now unquotes every name coming out of `parseJJBookmarks` before it's stored or
489	   compared, and `jjRebaseDestination` builds its revset from the raw bookmark name and remote, each
490	   quoted independently with `jjQuote`, rather than reusing the pre-joined `comparedTo` display string.
491	4. ~~**jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.**~~ **SHIPPED.** `parseJJBookmarks` now
492	   takes a `primaryRemote` hint (resolved from the configured remote list, ahead of the ref-derived
493	   merge) and picks that remote's row per bookmark name instead of last-write-wins, closing the
494	   `origin` + `upstream`-both-tracking-`main` collision.
495	5. ~~**`resolvedBranchNames` is stale-wins and never pruned.**~~ **SHIPPED.** The cache now yields
496	   instead of winning: `mergeLocalStatus` drops the entry when the sweep's `branchForCI` disagrees
497	   (`pruneResolvedBranchNameIfDrifted` — an empty/absent swept branch is not a disagreement, since a
498	   detached HEAD and an unbookmarked jj `@` legitimately report none), and `removeWorkroomLocally` /
499	   `removeProjectLocally` prune it on delete beside the label they already dropped. `git switch` in a
500	   workroom's terminal now follows within one sweep. Note what was NOT changed: the write side is still
501	   focused-target-only and still gated on the inspector showing Changes — that gate is the reason a read
502	   costs 2-3 processes rather than a pointer move, and drift-pruning is what makes it safe.
503	6. ~~**A failure is discarded if the selection moved.**~~ **SHIPPED.** The `lastFailure` write stays
504	   behind `finish`'s identity guard (correct — the bar renders whatever is selected NOW), but the DIALOG
505	   is now raised ahead of it, carrying `VCSFailureReport.workroom` so the sheet names where it happened
506	   when that isn't the current selection. Deliberately NOT a toast: `WorkroomNotification` is OSC-shaped
507	   (`targetID` + `tabID` + `kind == .osc`), so a VCS failure doesn't fit it without inventing a second
508	   kind, and the dialog was already the app's answer for "something you asked for failed" — it was just
509	   being suppressed.
510	7. ~~**A failed remote READ renders "No repository".**~~ **SHIPPED.** `RemoteStateModel` now publishes
511	   the read's failure typed (`readFailure`) rather than only as the `String` inside `state.failed`, which
512	   nothing rendered and nothing could classify. The presenter has a tier for it ([13b], below an action
513	   failure and an in-flight action, above everything else): it names the cause, carries the lock path,
514	   and — only when re-reading could plausibly help (`readRetryIsWorthwhile`) — offers "Try Again", which
515	   re-runs the READ (`retriesRead` — re-reading is not a `VCSRemoteAction`, so it can't route through
516	   `perform`). A read failure carrying an ACTION recovery (a leftover rebase, a rejection) offers that
517	   action instead; one that nothing can fix (`toolMissing`, a LOCATED lock, `noRemote`) is a disabled
518	   message, per `retryAction`'s rule. [13c] renders the re-read in flight ("Trying again…" + spinner).
519	   `activate` is wired too, as the toolbar's own `.task`.
520	8. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH".** `StatusCommandRunner`
521	   returns `commandNotFound` for a launch failure ("cwd vanished" per its own comment) and `classify`
522	   maps that exit code to `.toolMissing`, which offers no recovery — while the version toast
523	   simultaneously says git is fine. Launch failure needs its own sentinel.
524	9. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** The gate accepts
525	   re-admitting the original race past `maxChainWait`, justified as "the rare genuine-wedge case, not
526	   routine contention" — but fetch is budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so exceeding 30s is routine.
527	   Two windows, each with its own `AppStore` and its own `inFlight`, can queue two writes on one project
528	   root; the second gives up and runs concurrently with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`.
529	10. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** `classify` can hand a
530	    colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` from a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase` in its terminal, and
531	    the jj branch of `abortRebase` returns `.ok(summary: "Nothing to abort")` — so `finish` clears the

**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

### VCS toolbar: the findings the `/review` pass didn't fix (macapp)

**What:** Everything the toolbar review verified but left standing. Each was reproduced or read off the
code; none is speculative. Ordered by what a user hits first.

**Six have since SHIPPED and are struck below**, so the list is what remains:

- **the empty-remote case** (was (1)): `CLIVCSWriter.mergeRemotes` now unions the configured remote list
  (`git remote`, `jj git remote list`) with the ref-derived names for both backends, so publishing to a
  brand-new empty remote works and the counts stay ref-derived.
- **(5), (6) and (7)** — the three a user noticed — see each entry.

2. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Right for a workroom off trunk,
   wrong for one off a feature branch: it reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits and the rebase
   then refuses (`immutableHistory`, now typed and retry-free, so it fails honestly rather than looping).
   **Correction (2026-08-10): the "wrong for a feature branch" claim above does not reproduce.**
   Three ancestor-based revsets were tried against real jj repos while attempting a fix — `trunk() &
   ::@`, either-direction ancestry, and `(trunk()..@) & ::(immutable_heads())` — and all were falsified
   empirically; the last one was tested against a constructed feature-branch-with-independently-
   advancing-trunk scenario, and the real `jj rebase -b @ -d trunk()` command in that exact scenario
   **succeeded** (exit 0, "Rebased 2 commits to destination") rather than hitting
   `immutable_heads()`. jj's default `immutable_heads()` is `trunk()`-ancestors only — a merely-pushed
   feature bookmark isn't protected by it — which is likely why this entry's own measurement isn't
   reproducible from its stated recipe. Reopening this needs a fresh, documented repro (the exact repo
   shape and jj version that produced `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`), not another revset
   guess. The original "remember each workroom's own base" fix idea below is unaffected either way —
   it was already out of scope for a bug-fix pass (needs persistence + a migration path), independent
   of whether the triggering scenario reproduces.
   The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base rather than deriving it — `::@ &
   remote_bookmarks()` can't, because the base stops being an ancestor the moment it advances.
3. ~~**jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.**~~ **SHIPPED.** jj's template pre-quotes
   non-identifier names (verified: `"main|evil"` comes back WITH the quotes) — `jjUnquote` (the exact
   inverse of `jjQuote`) now unquotes every name coming out of `parseJJBookmarks` before it's stored or
   compared, and `jjRebaseDestination` builds its revset from the raw bookmark name and remote, each
   quoted independently with `jjQuote`, rather than reusing the pre-joined `comparedTo` display string.
4. ~~**jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.**~~ **SHIPPED.** `parseJJBookmarks` now
   takes a `primaryRemote` hint (resolved from the configured remote list, ahead of the ref-derived
   merge) and picks that remote's row per bookmark name instead of last-write-wins, closing the
   `origin` + `upstream`-both-tracking-`main` collision.
5. ~~**`resolvedBranchNames` is stale-wins and never pruned.**~~ **SHIPPED.** The cache now yields
   instead of winning: `mergeLocalStatus` drops the entry when the sweep's `branchForCI` disagrees
   (`pruneResolvedBranchNameIfDrifted` — an empty/absent swept branch is not a disagreement, since a
   detached HEAD and an unbookmarked jj `@` legitimately report none), and `removeWorkroomLocally` /
   `removeProjectLocally` prune it on delete beside the label they already dropped. `git switch` in a
   workroom's terminal now follows within one sweep. Note what was NOT changed: the write side is still
   focused-target-only and still gated on the inspector showing Changes — that gate is the reason a read
   costs 2-3 processes rather than a pointer move, and drift-pruning is what makes it safe.
6. ~~**A failure is discarded if the selection moved.**~~ **SHIPPED.** The `lastFailure` write stays
   behind `finish`'s identity guard (correct — the bar renders whatever is selected NOW), but the DIALOG
   is now raised ahead of it, carrying `VCSFailureReport.workroom` so the sheet names where it happened
   when that isn't the current selection. Deliberately NOT a toast: `WorkroomNotification` is OSC-shaped
   (`targetID` + `tabID` + `kind == .osc`), so a VCS failure doesn't fit it without inventing a second
   kind, and the dialog was already the app's answer for "something you asked for failed" — it was just
   being suppressed.
7. ~~**A failed remote READ renders "No repository".**~~ **SHIPPED.** `RemoteStateModel` now publishes
   the read's failure typed (`readFailure`) rather than only as the `String` inside `state.failed`, which
   nothing rendered and nothing could classify. The presenter has a tier for it ([13b], below an action
   failure and an in-flight action, above everything else): it names the cause, carries the lock path,
   and — only when re-reading could plausibly help (`readRetryIsWorthwhile`) — offers "Try Again", which
   re-runs the READ (`retriesRead` — re-reading is not a `VCSRemoteAction`, so it can't route through
   `perform`). A read failure carrying an ACTION recovery (a leftover rebase, a rejection) offers that
   action instead; one that nothing can fix (`toolMissing`, a LOCATED lock, `noRemote`) is a disabled
   message, per `retryAction`'s rule. [13c] renders the re-read in flight ("Trying again…" + spinner).
   `activate` is wired too, as the toolbar's own `.task`.
8. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH".** `StatusCommandRunner`
   returns `commandNotFound` for a launch failure ("cwd vanished" per its own comment) and `classify`
   maps that exit code to `.toolMissing`, which offers no recovery — while the version toast
   simultaneously says git is fine. Launch failure needs its own sentinel.
9. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** The gate accepts
   re-admitting the original race past `maxChainWait`, justified as "the rare genuine-wedge case, not
   routine contention" — but fetch is budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so exceeding 30s is routine.
   Two windows, each with its own `AppStore` and its own `inFlight`, can queue two writes on one project
   root; the second gives up and runs concurrently with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`.
10. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** `classify` can hand a
    colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` from a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase` in its terminal, and
    the jj branch of `abortRebase` returns `.ok(summary: "Nothing to abort")` — so `finish` clears the
    failure, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns.

8. ~~**A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH".**~~ **SHIPPED.**
   `CommandResult.launchFailed` (a negative sentinel, `-1`) is now returned by the runner's catch
   block instead of `commandNotFound` when the process never launched at all (cwd vanished), and

   reports "This workroom's folder is no longer there" instead of a false "tool missing" that
   contradicted the version toast.

   via a different mechanism than raising the ceiling.** Rather than raising `maxChainWait` (which
   would slow every unrelated status probe on the project, not just ones racing a live write), added
   a unified per-project `writingProjectRoots` counter (`ProjectStore`) that commit/fetch/push/pull
   all check via `isWritingProject`/`canStartWrite` BEFORE starting — a second write on the same
   project root now refuses outright (`.locked(nil)`, "The repository was busy. Try again.") instead
   of queuing into the gate and racing a live one past its wedge-detection ceiling. The gate's own
   30s ceiling is untouched — it still exists for a genuinely wedged single chain, which is a
   different problem.

    `abortRebase`'s jj branch now checks `rebaseInProgress(gitDir: worktreeGitDir(at: path))` before
    faking success — only a colocated root with no real git-side rebase state gets "Nothing to
    abort"; otherwise it falls through to a real `git rebase --abort` (explicitly against `"git"`,
    never the vcs-derived executable, which would run `jj` with git's flags and fail outright).

questions.question: Found a CRITICAL bug (confirmed independently by me + Testing specialist + Maintainability specialist, all three flagging the identical two lines): the new cross-window write-in-flight counter (writingProjectRoots, from T2) can get stuck at +1 forever if a window closes mid-write. performCommit's Task does `guard let self else { return }` BEFORE calling endWrite(); RemoteStateModel's Task calls `self?.writeDidFinish?(...)` with optional chaining. Either way, if the object (AppStore/RemoteStateModel) deallocates while a commit/fetch/push/pull is still running (e.g. user closes the window mid-push), the cleanup never runs. Since writingProjectRoots lives on the SHARED ProjectStore (all windows), this permanently refuses every future write for that project, in every window, with '.The repository was busy. Try again.' — until the app restarts. How should I fix it?

options.label: Decouple cleanup from self (recommended)
options.description: Capture `projectStore` strongly (not self) at the point each closure is wired/created, so the counter decrement always runs regardless of whether AppStore/RemoteStateModel still exist. Surgical: keeps weak-self everywhere else, no lifetime-extension side effects. Also fixes the identical pre-existing leak on committingProjectRoots while restructuring the same block (same root cause, same fix, right next to the new code).

options.label: Strong-self capture for these 2 Tasks
options.description: Simplest: drop [weak self] for just the commit/fetch/push/pull Tasks, so AppStore/RemoteStateModel can't deallocate until the write finishes. Correct behavior arguably (don't orphan a live git/jj process), but extends the closed window's AppStore lifetime up to the action's own timeout (300s for pull) — a real, if bounded, retention change worth deciding deliberately.

options.label: Ship as-is, track as known issue
options.description: Leave the leak in TODOS.md as a documented, narrow edge case (requires closing a window during an in-flight write) rather than fixing now. Lowest effort, but ships a real bug that silently disables VCS actions app-wide until relaunch, for anyone who hits it.

+  /// **The mechanism the write-in-flight leak fix depends on.** `AppStore.releaseWrite` must release
+  /// the mark against a `ProjectStore` directly, with no live `AppStore` involved at all — this is
+  /// what lets `performCommit`'s Task and `RemoteStateModel`'s `writeDidFinish` wiring release the
+  /// mark even after the `AppStore`/`RemoteStateModel` that started the write has already been
+  /// deallocated (e.g. the window closed mid-write). If this ever required a live `AppStore`, a
+  /// closed window mid-write would leak the mark forever and refuse every future write for that
+  /// project, in every window, until the app restarts.
+  func testReleaseWriteWorksAgainstAProjectStoreAloneNoAppStoreNeeded() {
+    let projectStore = ProjectStore()
+    projectStore.writingProjectRoots["/proj"] = 1
+    AppStore.releaseWrite(projectRoot: "/proj", in: projectStore)
+    XCTAssertNil(
+      projectStore.writingProjectRoots["/proj"],
+      "the mark must clear even though no AppStore instance was ever touched")
+  /// Two writes marked against the same root (defensive symmetry, mirrors `testEndWriteDecrements
+  /// RatherThanClears`): releasing must decrement, not clear outright, so a sibling write still in
+  /// flight isn't falsely freed.
+  func testReleaseWriteDecrementsRatherThanClears() {
+    let projectStore = ProjectStore()
+    projectStore.writingProjectRoots["/proj"] = 2
+    AppStore.releaseWrite(projectRoot: "/proj", in: projectStore)
+    XCTAssertEqual(projectStore.writingProjectRoots["/proj"], 1)
/// The common case: no other write in flight, so `performCommit` must proceed past the guard (it
/// marks `committingTargets`/`committingProjectRoots`/`writingProjectRoots` synchronously before

content.text:
**Pre-Landing Review: 6 issues (1 critical, 5 informational) — all fixed.**

This diff is uncommitted working-tree state on `master` (branch == base), covering the whole T1–T10 session: config-lock rewrite, write-in-flight gating, cache split, signal-classification fixes, jj bookmark/multi-remote fixes, and terminal accessibility. Dispatched Testing, Maintainability, and Security specialists (2243 macOS tests + 8 Go packages, all green; `swift-format lint --strict` clean).

**CRITICAL — fixed:** The new cross-window write-lock (`writingProjectRoots`) could leak permanently if a window closed mid-commit/fetch/push/pull — confirmed independently by me, the Testing specialist, and the Maintainability specialist, all flagging the identical two call sites. Fixed by decoupling the release from `self`'s lifetime (strong-captured `ProjectStore`, shared `AppStore.releaseWrite` helper) instead of gating it behind `guard let self`/`self?`.

**INFORMATIONAL — fixed:**
- TODOS.md was missing SHIPPED marks for 3 items this session actually shipped (launchFailed sentinel, write-lock, colocated-jj abortRebase) — stale header/priority line too.
- Dead code: `hasMissingTool(probedJJ:)`, zero callers after the cache-split rewrite.
- Stale comments (2 files) referencing `VCSToolVersionCache`'s removed `static let shared`.
- `AgentRunner.classify` didn't handle `.launchFailed` — a deleted-mid-action workroom rendered "exit -1" instead of a real message.
- Terminal accessibility exposed live content to any Accessibility-permitted process at any time, not just VoiceOver — now gated on `isVoiceOverEnabled` (or the test fixture), matching the feature's actual scope.

Added 4 new tests covering the fixes. Nothing committed — this all stays uncommitted per your standing "dev/nightly only" instruction.

fix(cli,macapp): close v2 GA bug/polish findings from VCS-foundation eng-review

CLI:
- internal/config: real OS advisory lock (gofrs/flock) replaces the hand-rolled
  O_CREATE|O_EXCL + mtime-staleness scheme, closing a real cross-process
  lost-update race with no elapsed-time heuristic to steal a live holder's lock.

macapp:
- Unified per-project write-in-flight refusal across commit/fetch/push/pull
  (writingProjectRoots on ProjectStore), so a second write on the same project
  root refuses outright instead of queuing into JJSnapshotGate and racing a
  live one past its wedge-detection ceiling. Fixed to release the mark even if
  the window closes mid-write (captured ProjectStore directly, not through a
  weak self/AppStore chain) — the original shape leaked the mark permanently
  on window-close, refusing every future write for that project forever.
- Colocated jj root's abortRebase now runs a real `git rebase --abort` instead
  of unconditionally faking success, closing an inescapable retry loop.
- CommandResult gets a distinct launchFailed sentinel (-1) for a vanished cwd,
  separate from commandNotFound (127) — a deleted-mid-action workroom no
  longer misreports "git isn't on PATH". Wired into VCSWriting, AgentRunner,
  and TerminalAgentManager's classifiers.
- VCSToolVersionCache split into independent git/jj slots (GitHubAuthCache
  shape: freshness lease, generation-stamped in-flight, instance ownership),
  closing a reentrancy bug where a jj-blind probe could clobber a jj-aware
  cached verdict, and letting a stale .belowFloor clear without a relaunch.
- CommandResult.signaled consumed in three remaining sites (AgentRunner,
  FileTreeModel, RustJJProvider) so a killed process is never misread as a
  real exit code or a "not a repo" state.
- jj bookmark names needing revset quoting (e.g. containing `|`) now match:
  jjUnquote (jjQuote's exact inverse) unquotes names out of parseJJBookmarks,
  and jjRebaseDestination builds its revset from quoted (name, remote) pairs
  instead of a pre-joined display string.
- jj multi-remote tracking: parseJJBookmarks now picks the primary remote's
  row instead of last-write-wins when multiple remotes track one bookmark.
- Terminal content is now really exposed to VoiceOver (accessibilityValue,
  accessibilitySelectedText, throttled change notifications), not just the
  UI-test fixture — gated on NSWorkspace.isVoiceOverEnabled so it doesn't
  publish to every Accessibility-permitted process at all times. Verified
  against a real echo-disabled password prompt that no typed content leaks.

Investigated and reverted: jj Pull's trunk() guess for an unbookmarked `@`.
Three ancestor-based revsets were tried and each falsified against real jj
repos — the last one's "known failure" scenario succeeded when actually run
(jj rebase -b @ -d trunk(), exit 0). No reproducible bug survives, so nothing
shipped there; TODOS.md corrected to say so.

1	# TODOs
2	
3	> Grouped by priority, then by area. Within a group, cheaper/higher-leverage first. Each entry states
4	> what it is, why, how to start, what it depends on, and its priority. Completed work is summarised in
5	> **Recently done** at the bottom — including the traps found while doing it, which are the parts worth
6	> reading before touching the same code. Full write-ups for finished items live in git history.
7	
8	## P1 — before GA
9	
10	### Terminal *content* accessibility (macapp) — CMT-3 — SHIPPED (2026-08-10)
11	
12	**Shipped:** `isAccessibilityElement()`/`accessibilityValue()` are real now (no longer gated behind
13	the UI-test fixture), a new `accessibilitySelectedText()` reads the existing `readSelectionText()`,
14	and a 400ms `Timer` poll posts coalesced `.valueChanged`/`.selectedTextChanged` only when the read
15	content actually changed. There is no render/damage callback on the libghostty side to hook instead
16	(checked `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`'s full `GHOSTTY_ACTION_*` switch first) — the poll checks
17	`NSWorkspace.shared.isVoiceOverEnabled` FIRST on every tick, so the real cost (materializing the
18	viewport into a `String`) is paid only while VoiceOver is actually listening. The safety property
19	below (a password prompt must never leak through this) was verified empirically, not by reasoning
20	about terminal semantics: `TerminalAccessibilityUITests.testPasswordPromptWithEchoDisabledRendersNoTypedCharacters`
21	drives a real `stty -echo` + `read` prompt in a real pane and asserts the typed secret never appears
22	in the read viewport. Everything below this line is the pre-fix scoping and stays as the historical
23	record of what was decided and why.
24	
25	**What:** VoiceOver support for the terminal's *rendered text* on `GhosttySurfaceView` — accessible
26	value (screen text), selected text, and change notifications — so the terminal content is navigable
27	with assistive tech.
28	
29	**Done so far:** the **UI-tree** a11y has landed (commit `f3859f9`) — `PaneTreeView` exposes each
30	leaf as `terminal.pane` with a label ("Terminal <title>, pane N of M"), a focused/selected trait, and
31	an adjustable split divider (`pane.grip`). That claim is unqualified: the one caveat raised against it
32	(the tab strips' glyph buttons reporting `isHittable == false`) was investigated and closed as an
33	XCUITest artefact — see **Recently done**. What's still missing is the *content* layer: the
34	libghostty surface is Metal-rendered, so its text is pixels — invisible to the accessibility system.
35	Today the surface view sets `role=.textArea` + a label only; it exposes **no value and no selection**,
36	so VoiceOver reads nothing inside the terminal. Accepted regression for the beta (CMT-3). This is also
37	the **enabler for content-level UI tests**: once terminal text is in the a11y tree, XCUITest can
38	assert on rendered output (backspace deleted, TUI drew, scrollback) on top of the now-landed fixture
39	seam — see `macapp/QA-libghostty.md` (Bucket 2).
40	
41	**When:** feasible on the currently pinned engine today (the read APIs exist), but ghostty upstream
42	has merged a11y plumbing worth riding — **ghostty #12902** ("core: send selection_changed
43	notification", merged 2026-06-04), which on macOS posts `.ghosttySelectionDidChange` → debounced →
44	`NSAccessibility.selectedTextChanged`. On the pinned engine we'd have to post that notification
45	ourselves from our own selection events; after the pin bump it comes from the engine as
46	`GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED`.
47	
48	This is unblocked by the **pin bump** (see "Bump the libghostty pin", P2), NOT by owning the
49	xcframework — an earlier version of this entry sequenced it behind CMT-2, which was wrong. A
50	before-GA item either way; doing it before the bump costs one self-posted notification.
51	
52	**How to start (minimal-viable, keep light per D1 — crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`):**
53	- `accessibilityValue()` → visible screen text via `ghostty_surface_read_text(surface, <viewport
54	  ghostty_selection_s>, …)` (reuse the `extractString(from:)` helper).
55	- `accessibilitySelectedText()` → `ghostty_surface_read_selection` (the same read that powers
56	  copy-on-select).
57	- Post `NSAccessibility.post(element:notification:)` `.selectedTextChanged` on selection change
58	  (we already detect mouseUp / copy-on-select) and a throttled `.valueChanged` on output so
59	  VoiceOver follows along; keep the role/label and report focus.
60	- Skip the full `NSAccessibility` text protocol (line/char-range/bounds geometry) — overkill for a
61	  terminal, and Muxy keeps it minimal too.
62	
63	**Caveat:** terminal a11y is inherently partial (dynamic output, scrollback, full-screen TUIs);
64	target "announce output + selection, navigable text", not a perfect document model.
65	
66	**Depends on:** the read APIs already present in the pinned engine (`ghostty_surface_read_selection`,
67	`ghostty_surface_read_text`, `extractString`) in `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`.
68	Cheaper after the pin bump (engine-sent `selection_changed`), but not blocked by it.
69	
70	**Priority:** P2 (accessibility regression — address before GA, not blocking the beta).
71	
72	### Every shipped beta has an arm64-only CLI inside a universal app (macapp) — FIXED IN TREE, UNRELEASED
73	
74	**What:** the app is universal; the `workroom` CLI it bundles is arm64-only. Verified on the
75	published `v2.0.0-beta.23` DMG:
76	
77	```
78	Workroom.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom      x86_64 arm64
79	Workroom.app/Contents/Resources/workroom  arm64        ← thin
80	```
81	
82	**Why it matters:** the app drives *every* workroom operation through that binary
83	(`create`/`list`/`delete`/`add-project`/`delete-project --json`). On an Intel Mac the app launches,
84	renders, and then fails at all of it. Rosetta does not help — that translates the other direction.
85	
86	**Cause:** `ARCHS` is a space-separated list (`"arm64 x86_64"`), and `build-helper.sh` matched it as
87	a single token, falling through to a `warn:`-and-default-to-arm64 branch. The warning was buried in
88	xcodebuild output; codesign, notarization and Gatekeeper are all happy with a thin nested binary.
89	Present since `8bae1b2a` (2026-06-02), the commit that added the app — so beta.1 through beta.23.
90	The standalone CLI's own `darwin_amd64` tarball was always fine; only the embedded copy was thin.
91	
92	**Fixed** in `build-helper.sh` (per-arch build + `lipo`), asserted at release time by
93	`release.sh check_universal()`, and regression-tested by `macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh`
94	(proven to fail against the old logic). **Not yet released.**
95	
96	**Open decision:** whether this warrants cutting a beta ahead of the normal cadence. It has been
97	broken for two months, so urgency is lower than severity suggests — but any Intel user who has
98	tried the app has a broken install.
99	
100	**Priority:** P2 — fixed, pending a release decision.
101	
102	## P2 — perf, correctness, and the next VCS phase
103	
104	### Bump the libghostty pin (macapp) — post-GA, first change after the GA tag
105	
106	**What:** move `macapp/project.yml` from the currently pinned `libghostty-spm` package to **1.3.2**
107	(ghostty commit `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`). Those two numbers are this task's
108	TARGET, not a claim about what ships — for what is pinned today, read `project.yml`'s comment, which
109	is the single source of truth. Re-check the target against the packager's newest release before
110	starting; it moves.
111	
112	**Why:** it is the only way to reach `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid` + `ghostty_surface_tty_name`
113	(the "libghostty exposes no PTY child PID" limitation CMT-1 records at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:95`)
114	and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (CMT-3's a11y hook), plus ~1300 upstream commits. **It ships
115	no user-visible change by itself** — both wins need separate work to wire — which is exactly why it
116	waits for GA rather than riding under it.
117	
118	**The version trap that produced two wrong roadmap entries — read this first.** `libghostty-spm`
119	versions its **package** independently of ghostty. The release bodies state the ghostty ref
120	explicitly, and package `1.2.3` is built from ghostty **`v1.3.1`**. Reading a package version as a
121	ghostty version is what made an earlier CMT-2 claim we trailed ghostty by ~2 versions and file it as
122	P1. Package `1.3.1` ≠ ghostty `v1.3.1`. Always read `Ghostty.ref` + the release body, never the tag.
123	
124	**The real risk is the patch swap, not the API.** The packager applies its own patches to ghostty
125	before building, and `Script/apply-patches.sh` feature-probes the header to choose between them:
126	
127	```
128	  grep -q "ghostty_surface_foreground_pid" include/ghostty.h
129	      │
130	      ├── absent  (ghostty v1.3.1 — what we ship today)
131	      │     └── 0002-host-managed-io.patch          (17,588 B)
132	      │
133	      └── present (ghostty 35e1a016 — package 1.3.2)
134	            └── 0002-host-managed-io-modern.patch   (18,447 B)   ← never run here
135	                                                                    PTY/IO hosting: surface teardown,
136	                                                                    orphan shells, the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
137	                                                                    site WorkroomApp.swift:606 documents
138	```
139	
140	By contrast the mid-enum `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` insert — which renumbers 14 following
141	tags including `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` and `COMMAND_FINISHED` — is **not** a risk: header and static
142	archive ship together, `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` dispatches on symbolic labels, and
143	nothing persists a raw tag. Don't spend the retest budget there. (Don't write a test asserting a
144	tag's raw value either — test and app import the same header, so it can never fail.)
145	
146	**Blocking work, same commit:**
147	- ~~**Decide the `ghostty +ssh` question.**~~ **DONE, ahead of this bump.**
148	  `Contents/MacOS/ghostty` is now a relative symlink to the app binary, and `main.swift` dispatches
149	  Ghostty's `+action` CLI on `argv[0]` — libghostty already carried the whole action set, so no
150	  second binary and no Zig toolchain were needed. `GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR` turned out to be set by the
151	  engine all along (from the running executable's directory); the directory simply had no `ghostty`
152	  in it. Full correction in `Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md`. **Regenerating `shell-integration/` is
153	  now safe — but only with or after this bump**, never before it: `+ssh` does not exist at the
154	  pinned v1.3.1 and arrives at the bump target.
155	- **Test `+ssh` itself, not just `+ssh-cache`.** After regeneration the wrapper *is* `ghostty +ssh`,
156	  with no `infocmp` fallback branch left — so a failure there is total, not degraded, and silent
157	  either way. The `+ssh-cache` tests that shipped with the ghostty symlink (`GhosttyCLITests`) all
158	  pass with `+ssh` broken or absent, because they exercise a different action. Required with the
159	  regeneration: a dispatch test (`ghostty +ssh --help` exits 0, asserted on the shipped artifact the
160	  way `release.sh` already asserts `+ssh-cache`) **and** a shell-wrapper integration test that
161	  actually `ssh`es through the regenerated script to a real host.
162	- **Regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/`** from the same ghostty ref — `terminfo/` and
163	  `shell-integration/` ONLY, then refresh `CHECKSUMS` (`shasum -a 256`, see
164	  `GhosttyResourcesTests`) and rewrite the provenance section of `SOURCE.md`. `themes/` is ours and
165	  must not be touched. Note the current resources are *ahead* of the pinned engine, not behind — the
166	  measured detail is in `SOURCE.md`, and a regeneration must not silently drop the four upstream
167	  script fixes recorded there.
168	- **Resolve `TerminalSearch.navigationPlan`.** It both inverts direction against the engine's
169	  ordering and synthesizes wrap by emitting `total - 1` steps, keyed to the pinned engine's "stops
170	  dead at the ends" behaviour. If wrapping or match ordering moved upstream, ⌘G becomes *wrong*, not
171	  redundant.
172	
173	**Retest the IO layer, not the enum:** repeated surface create/destroy, split/close churn, workroom
174	switch/delete, the run-tab supervisor, and the `ps` orphan check. `0010-fix-scroll-remainder-zeroing.patch`
175	is also new, so include the scrollbar overlay. The XCUITest action-tag baseline (added ahead of this
176	work, deliberately against the old engine) is the pass/fail gate.
177	
178	**Also required:**
179	- **A universal Release build before landing.** ~~CI only ever builds Debug/arm64, so the first
180	  universal link happens at release time.~~ **That was wrong** — `nightly.yml` has run
181	  `make app-release` (universal Rust core + `ARCHS_STANDARD` Release) daily since it landed. What
182	  was actually missing was an *assertion*, which now exists: `release.sh` refuses to notarize a
183	  bundle containing any thin Mach-O. So the bump inherits a daily universal build plus a gate; run
184	  one locally only if you want the signal before pushing:
185	  `VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs`, then
186	  `xcodebuild -configuration Release ARCHS="arm64 x86_64" ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO build`.
187	- **A bake gate.** `nightly.yml` builds daily from master, so this reaches nightly users ~24h after
188	  landing. Require N clean nightlies before it enters a `pre` tag.
189	- **A `QA-libghostty.md` §N "engine bump smoke"** (~12 items). Committing to the full 13-section
190	  manual walk on every bump guarantees it won't happen next time.
191	
192	**Rollback is not one line:** revert the commit(s), `rm -rf macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages`,
193	rebuild. CI's `spm-`/`xcbuild-` caches key on `project.yml` and their `restore-keys` fallback can
194	restore a mixed state. Do **not** remove any workaround (backspace DEL-as-text, ⌃Tab) until this has
195	baked — both fail safe, and the backspace test passes either way, so removal needs a raw-PTY probe.
196	
197	**Depends on:** GA shipping first. `Package.resolved` is now tracked, so the resolved revision is a
198	reviewable diff.
199	
200	**Priority:** P2 — real value, no user-visible gain on its own, and it swaps the layer that runs the
201	user's shell. First change after the GA tag, not before it.
202	
203	### Own the GhosttyKit xcframework (macapp) — CMT-2, GA-time supply-chain decision
204	
205	**What:** stop depending on the third-party `libghostty-spm` (Lakr233) package as the source of
206	truth. Build our own universal `GhosttyKit.xcframework` + version-matched resources from a ghostty
207	ref *we* pin, and point `project.yml` at it.
208	
209	**Status: demoted from P1, and re-argued.** Two of the three rationales this entry used to carry were
210	wrong, and are struck:

339	### VCS write actions — Phase 2 (macapp) — roadmap pointer
340	
341	**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. **Fetch, push
342	and pull-with-rebase have SHIPPED** (the VCS toolbar), and so have **commit + message-only amend/describe**
343	(the Changes inspector's commit dialog). What remains: selection-aware amend (needs a temp index),
344	bookmark (jj) / branch (git) management, and the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog,
345	interdiff).
346	
347	**Where the write seam actually is — this changed.** The original plan put write methods on
348	`VCSProviding` with a `CLIVCSProvider` fallback. That is **not** what shipped, and new work should not
349	follow it. Writes live behind a **separate** `VCSWriting` protocol (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) with its
350	own factory `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by `CLIVCSWriter`. Two reasons, both load-bearing:
351	
352	- `VCSProviding`'s doc calls it "the single seam the app **reads** VCS data through", and four
353	  resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no gate. A `fetch` on that protocol means
354	  nothing structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation — the opposite of what
355	  `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee.
356	- A CLI-backed method needs an injected `StatusCommandRunning`, and `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are
357	  stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one. A new conformer has
358	  somewhere.
359	
360	So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
361	environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.
362	
363	**Which backend each op uses — decided, don't re-litigate.** `VCSWriting` says *where* writes live,
364	not *how* they run. The split:
365	
366	| Ops | Backend | Why |
367	|---|---|---|
368	| commit/amend — **CLI, decided against this table's original answer** | **CLI** (`CLIVCSWriter.commit`, shipped) | This row used to say "native", and that was wrong on three counts it never weighed. **libgit2 runs no hooks** ([#964](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/issues/964)) — a `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` that the user's terminal honours would be silently skipped, which is worse than not offering commit at all. **libgit2 cannot sign**, so `commit.gpgsign = true` would produce unsigned commits. And native jj commit is blocked on `immutable_heads()` being a jj-*cli* revset alias that jj-lib cannot resolve — so it would happily rewrite commits the user's own `jj` refuses to touch. (The empty-committer and dropped-signature halves of that third blocker are now fixed by `jj_config.rs`; the revset one is not.) |
369	| branch + bookmark management, jj undo/op-log/split/absorb/evolog | **native** (libgit2/SwiftGitX, jj-lib) — provisional | Local, typed APIs, no output to parse, no tool-version floor, no locale exposure. Still the default answer, but **not "don't re-litigate"**: commit was re-litigated on measurement and moved. Check each op for hooks, signing, and revset aliases before assuming native. |
370	| fetch, push, pull | **CLI** — permanently, not a stopgap | Three independent blockers, all verified from checked-out sources: SwiftGitX passes NULL options (`git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)`, and `pull` is a `// TODO`), so it has no credential callback at all; **libgit2 implements no `credential.helper` protocol** — nothing in its `src` reads that config key, so native auth means reimplementing helper invocation ourselves; and jj-lib shells to `git` for remote ops anyway (that's where its `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION` comes from), so a "native jj push" is a git subprocess wearing a Rust coat. |
371	
372	**Non-goal: Workroom does not store credentials.** No OAuth client, no keychain writes, no auth
373	prompt, no account concept. The user's own helpers (`osxkeychain`, GCM, `!gh auth git-credential`,
374	anything corporate) are the correct answer, and shelling out gets every host — including ones we've
375	never heard of — for free, with the same credentials their terminal uses. GitHub Desktop is the
376	instructive counterexample: it also shells out (via `dugite`, which bundles its own git), but blanks
377	your helpers and registers itself as `credential.helper=desktop` because being *the GitHub client* is
378	its product. The cost of that choice is `app/src/lib/generic-git-auth.ts` — a second credential store,
379	with its own prompt UI, keychain keys and invalidation, for every non-GitHub host. We are not that
380	product, and the app's one GitHub dependency (PR status) already rides `gh`'s own token.
381	
382	**When you do shell out, never parse prose.** `--porcelain`, `-z`, `%(…)`, `-T`, exit codes. Measured:
383	`Updates were rejected` becomes `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées` under `fr_FR.UTF-8`, so a prose
384	match loses the whole failure taxonomy for a non-English user. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C`
385	as a backstop; it is not the plan.
386	
387	*Filed, not planned:* bundling our own `git` the way `dugite` does would delete all of
388	`Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` — floor, probe, notification, per-VCS scoping. Real cost (universal
389	binary, notarization, ~40MB, and the Go CLI would want the same binary), so revisit only if the
390	version floor actually bites a user.
391	
392	**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up. The authoritative scope + sequencing live
393	in the issue #59 plan; this entry is the pointer that makes it discoverable.

395	**How to start:** Read `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — its doc comment carries the routing diagram, the

407	### `withTimeout` doesn't observe the CALLER's own cancellation (macapp) — VCS-foundation eng-review, /review follow-up
408	
409	**Status:** the original version of this entry (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` awaiting a detached
410	operation child past its own deadline) is **fixed** — `Core/Timeout.swift` now races via a single
411	`withCheckedThrowingContinuation` + a `TimeoutGate`, exactly the fix this entry used to recommend.
412	Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
413	and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam.
414	
415	**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
416	(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
417	`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
418	Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
419	old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
420	child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
421	to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
422	enclosing task gave up.
423	
424	**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
425	fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
426	caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). This is a
427	responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one, because the call sites in this seam do
428	check `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result (`runLocalSweep`'s
429	`if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.).
430	
431	**Corrected 2026-08-05 — do NOT re-read this entry as "the convention protects us".** This used to
432	say *every* call site already checks, so state stays correct. That was false, and the counterexample
433	shipped: `refreshGitHubCLI` mutated `githubCLIStatus` **inside** an awaited function, where the
434	callers' own guards (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:86`/`:144`) run too late to help. A cancelled
435	probe's SIGKILLed `gh` still returned through `StatusCommandRunner`'s non-throwing continuation with
436	the signal number as its exit code, the classifier read that as "not signed in", and publishing it
437	*stamped the TTL* — so the wrong value suppressed its own repair for a full minute. The cost of a
438	missed guard is therefore a **wrong published value**, not merely a wasted probe. Two defences
439	landed with that fix and are what keeps the residual risk low: `CommandResult.signaled` (a killed
440	child is never mistaken for a CLI that ran and failed) and `GHAuthProbe.keepPrior` (a non-answer
441	neither writes nor stamps). The `withTimeout` gap below is a genuinely different mechanism and stays
442	deferred on its own merits.
443	
444	**How to start:** Wrap `withTimeout`'s continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so cancelling
445	the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to
446	propagate cancellation into its own chained `Task`). Verify the existing "operation keeps running,
447	result dropped" contract still holds — this only makes the WAIT responsive to cancellation, not the
448	underlying synchronous native call (still uncancellable, unchanged).
449	
450	**Depends on:** —. Touches `Core/Timeout.swift`. Broad blast radius (every `withTimeout` caller:
451	`WorkroomStatusResolver`, `BranchResolver`, `JJSnapshotGate`'s own internal use) — needs its own
452	careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix.
453	
454	**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

542	a terminal". It doesn't, for the terminals this app opens — a fetch inside a worktree writes
543	`worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` while the common one stays put (measured), so counts update from the shared
544	`refs/remotes` while the timestamp doesn't. Either read both and take the max, or stop claiming it.
545	
546	**Why:** These are the residue of a five-pass review (critical + 4 specialists + Claude adversarial +
547	Codex) whose P0s — argv option injection and jj push publishing the wrong workspace's commit — are
548	already fixed. What's left is real but none of it is a security hole or silent data loss.
549	
550	**Priority:** P2. What remains is (2) alone, and even that isn't open work in the usual sense — see
551	its 2026-08-10 correction above: the scenario it describes doesn't reproduce, so there's nothing left
552	to fix without a fresh, documented repro first. Everything else in this list has shipped.
553	
554	### Gate git VCS *reads*, not just writes (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
555	
556	**What:** Route git status reads through the same per-project `JJSnapshotGate` the writes now use.
557	
558	**Why:** The toolbar's write path gates git as well as jj, because a project's workrooms are
559	`git worktree add` worktrees sharing ONE `.git` — a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a workroom
560	wedged in a rebase. But that only half-closes the contention: `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`
561	never touches the gate (only `resolveJJ` does), so a fetch writing `packed-refs` while the ungated
562	status sweep runs `git status` across N sibling worktrees reproduces exactly the
563	`packed-refs.lock could not be obtained` failure the gate's own doc cites.
564	
565	**Pros:** removes the last window where `.locked` is an *expected* outcome rather than an anomaly, so
566	the UI's Retry affordance becomes a genuine edge case.
567	
568	**Cons:** serialising reads could measurably slow the status sweep, which fans out per workroom by
569	design. This wants measurement first — it may be that read/write contention is rare enough in practice
570	that the cost isn't worth it.
571	
572	**Context / how to start:** `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (the ungated read) vs `resolveJJ` (the
573	gated one); `CLIVCSWriter.gated` for how the writes do it. Note the gate is key-based and
574	backend-agnostic, so if this lands, renaming `JJSnapshotGate` → `RepoWriteGate` (3 call sites + its
575	test suite) stops being speculative churn and starts being accurate.
576	
577	**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
578	
579	**Priority:** P3 (a real but narrow race; needs measurement before it's worth the sweep's latency).
580	
581	### jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
582	
583	**What:** Detect and surface when a jj operation in one workroom leaves a *sibling* workspace stale.
584	
585	**Why:** All workrooms of a jj project share one repo and op-store. `jj rebase -b @` — what
586	pull-with-rebase runs — rewrites commits, and any other workspace whose `@` descends from a rewritten
587	commit is marked stale and needs `jj workspace update-stale` before its next command. Today that
588	surfaces as an unexplained error in a **different** workroom from the one the user acted in, which is
589	the worst attribution problem available: nothing on screen connects cause to effect.
590	
591	**Pros:** turns a mystery error into an explained one, and the repair is a single command Workroom
592	could offer as a button.
593	
594	**Cons:** needs a cheap way to detect staleness across workspaces without reading each one (a per-op
595	check would multiply the cost of every pull).
596	
597	**Context / how to start:** `VCSStatusFailure.staleWorkingCopy` already exists in the taxonomy, and
598	`RustJJProvider.workingStatus` already maps jj's stale-working-copy error onto it — so the detection
599	half may largely exist; the gap is noticing it for a workroom the user is NOT looking at, and offering
600	the repair. The repair is itself a write, so it belongs on `VCSWriting`.
601	
602	**Depends on:** pull-with-rebase (shipped).
603	
604	**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; wrong-workroom errors are rare but very confusing).
605	
606	### jj `push-<id>` bookmarks accumulate on the remote (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
607	
608	**What:** Decide what happens to the `push-<change-id>` bookmarks that pushing an unbookmarked jj `@`
609	leaves on the remote.
610	
611	**Why:** A jj workroom is `jj workspace add`, whose `@` carries no bookmark, so the toolbar's Push runs
612	`jj git push --change @`. jj creates a bookmark named by `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
613	`"push-" ++ change_id.short()`), and **nothing ever removes it**. Verified on jj 0.43 against a bare
614	origin — two pushes of two different changes left two bookmarks behind permanently:
615	
616	```
617	push-rrxukuporqwy
618	push-slxllnxlmxwz
619	```
620	
621	On a shared remote that accrues indefinitely, one entry per change anyone ever pushed from a workroom.
622	
623	**Not a problem, though it was filed as one:** the review paired this with a suspected
624	non-fast-forward asymmetry — that re-pushing an amended change would be rejected. It isn't. A change id
625	is stable across amends, so jj moves its own bookmark with no force flag and no error:
626	
627	```
628	bookmark: push-slxllnxlmxwz [move sideways from b7e44fc98f79 to 8f82f551ad69]
629	```
630	
631	Don't re-investigate that half.
632	
633	**Pros:** a shared remote stays legible.
634	
635	**Cons:** this is jj's OWN behaviour for an anonymous push, not something Workroom invented — bare
636	`jj git push --change` does exactly this. Diverging from it means inventing a naming or cleanup policy
637	that jj users won't expect from other jj tools. Doing nothing is defensible.
638	
639	**Context / how to start:** `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision` and the `--change` push path; the options are
640	(a) leave it and document it, (b) offer cleanup of merged `push-*` bookmarks, or (c) require a bookmark
641	before pushing, which costs the one-click Publish a fresh workroom currently gets.
642	
643	**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
644	
645	**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; cosmetic on a personal remote, untidy on a shared one — and the
646	status quo matches jj's own).
647	
648	### "New workroom from branch…" (macapp) — the successor to branch switching
649	
650	**What:** Pick a local or remote branch and create a workroom for it, from the VCS toolbar's branch
651	segment or the ⌘O picker.
652	
653	**Why:** Branch *switching* was deliberately cut from the VCS toolbar. A workroom's identity IS its
654	branch — `internal/vcs/git.go` creates it with `git worktree add -b`, and there is no `branch` field
655	anywhere in `internal/config` — so switching a workroom's branch makes its directory name permanently
656	wrong, with nothing to reconcile the two. The jj equivalent is worse: `jj new <bookmark>` on the
657	bookmark the toolbar already displays was reproduced **removing a file from the working copy** and
658	leaving the workroom's commit as a nameless dangling head, with no visible change in the UI.
659	
660	But the underlying need — "I want to work on that other branch" — is real, and creating a workroom is
661	the answer the product model actually supports. The toolbar's branch segment is **display only** — it
662	briefly routed to ⌘O, which was dropped because ⌘O lists only workrooms that already exist, so the
663	click promised more than it delivered. That leaves the segment with no action at all, which is the
664	honest state until this lands and gives it one worth having.
665	
666	**Pros:** gives the cut affordance a correct home; makes an existing remote branch a first-class
667	starting point instead of requiring a manual create-then-checkout.
668	
669	**Cons:** needs a branch list (the toolbar deliberately stopped enumerating refs when the picker was
670	cut), and a naming policy for the new workroom.
671	
672	**Context / how to start:** `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` is the searchable, project-grouped picker
673	to clone; the Go CLI's `create` already accepts a branch. `CLIVCSWriter.gitRemoteRefsArgs` shows how to
674	enumerate remote refs cheaply, and its doc explains why the symref row must be dropped.
675	
676	**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
677	
678	**Priority:** P3 (a real gap, but ⌘O plus a terminal covers it today).
679	
680	## P3 — VCS engine, diffs, and status
681	
682	### `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` never reaches the `gh` auth probe (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up
683	
684	**What:** decide whether `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or another way of resolving gh's config dir) should reach
685	the NON-network `run` path that `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGitHubCLI` uses.
686	
687	**Why:** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` *is* in `StatusCommandRunner.forwardedAuthKeys`, but that allowlist is only
688	applied by `networkEnvironment`, i.e. behind `if network` in `run`. The gh auth probe is a plain `run`,
689	and the comment justifying the split says gh "carries its own token" — true, but gh FINDS that token via
690	its config dir. A user who sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in `.zshrc` and launches from Finder therefore hands
691	gh a different config root than their terminal uses. Measured: an empty gh config dir returns
692	`{"hosts":{}}` on stdout with exit 0, which classifies as `.notAuthenticated` — a permanent false
693	"GitHub CLI not signed in" for someone who is signed in everywhere else. Same false claim the
694	cancelled-probe fix removed, reached by a completely different route.
695	
696	**Pros:** closes the last known cause of a false "not signed in". **Cons:** widening the environment on
697	an automatic path is a deliberate, documented narrowness (`StatusCommandRunner` explains why a
698	wholesale transplant is refused for anything that runs without the user asking) — this is a security
699	posture question, not a one-line fix. A third allowlist ("non-secret, both paths") is probably the right
700	shape, and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` deserves the same thought.
701	
702	**How to start:** `StatusCommandRunner.run`, where `if network` selects the environment. Decide the
703	allowlist question first, then apply to both paths.
704	
705	**Depends on:** nothing.
706	
707	**Priority:** P3 — real and measured, but it needs a policy decision, and the affected configuration is
708	uncommon.
709	
710	### The other `CommandResult` consumers don't know about `signaled` (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up
711	
712	**What:** consume `CommandResult.signaled` in `AgentRunner.classify`, `FileTreeModel`, and
713	`RustJJProvider.runCLI`.
714	
715	**Why:** the gh-flap fix added `signaled` (a killed child reports its SIGNAL in `terminationStatus`, so
716	9 or 15 is not an exit code) and wired it into the gh classifiers plus both `CLIVCSWriter` failure
717	classifiers. Three consumers still read a raw exit code as evidence. `AgentRunner.classify` is the one
718	that reaches a user: a killed `claude` diagnosis becomes `.failed(exitCode: 9)` and the agent banner
719	shows "exit 9", which is exactly the class of nonsense commit `a64e4269` set out to end.
720	`FileTreeModel` gates on `result.ok`, so a signalled listing renders as a silently empty file tree.
721	`RustJJProvider` throws `VCSError.io("jj exited 9")`.
722	
723	**Pros:** finishes the job — every place that reads an exit code as evidence learns that a signal is not
724	one. Each site is a one-line branch plus a test, since the mechanism already exists and is tested.
725	**Cons:** none of the three has a reported symptom, and two fail safe (an empty tree, a typed IO error)
726	rather than making a false claim.
727	
728	**How to start:** `AgentRunner.classify` first (the only user-visible one): treat `signaled` as its own
729	outcome before the `exitCode != 0` branch, and mind that `timedOut` implies `signaled`, so the timeout
730	check must stay first.
731	
732	**Depends on:** `CommandResult.signaled` (shipped).
733	
734	**Priority:** P3 — cheap, but speculative until someone reports one.
735	
736	### `ShellEnvironment` exposes no probe-readiness signal (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up
737	
738	**What:** give `ShellEnvironment` a way for callers to know whether the interactive-shell PATH probe has
739	landed (or to await it), instead of silently degrading to the floor.
740	
741	**Why:** `ShellEnvironment.path()` returns the probed PATH if the probe finished and the deterministic
742	floor otherwise, with nothing distinguishing the two. The probe is fired detached in `WorkroomApp.init`
743	and nothing joins it, while `refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` — so a launch-time
744	`--version` probe can genuinely run against floor-only PATH. The floor covers Homebrew but not a
745	version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts, so those tools read as missing. `VCSToolVersionCache` no
746	longer *pins* such a verdict (it refuses to cache a discovered absence — shipped with the gh-flap work),
747	but that treats the symptom: any future caller reading `path()` early inherits the same ambiguity with
748	no way to detect it.
749	
750	**Pros:** removes a whole class of "it depends when we asked" bugs, and would let the few callers that
751	genuinely need enrichment await it rather than guess. **Cons:** the probe is best-effort BY DESIGN — its
752	failures must degrade to the floor, never block — so a readiness signal must not become a hidden
753	dependency that stalls launch. Larger and more delicate than it first looks.
754	
755	**How to start:** `ShellEnvironment.ProbeState` already tracks a generation; surface "has a probe
756	completed" from it, then audit `path()` callers for who should wait versus who should keep degrading.
757	
758	**Depends on:** nothing.
759	
760	**Priority:** P3 — the honest fix for a family of PATH-timing bugs, none currently reported.
761	
762	### `VCSToolVersionCache` pins a tool verdict for the whole process (macapp) — gh-flap follow-up
763	
764	**What:** give the `git`/`jj` version cache the three contracts the `gh` cache got in the same area and
765	this one never did: a freshness lease, a generation-stamped in-flight slot, and per-`ProjectStore`
766	ownership instead of `static let shared`. `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` (the cache is the actor at the
767	bottom); the shape to copy is `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift`.
768	
769	**Why (the user-visible half first):** `report(probeJJ:)` caches every verdict except `.notInstalled`
770	**forever** — the only thing that clears `cached` is the tests-only `reset()`. So `.belowFloor` is
771	permanent for the process: the user reads "Git 2.41 or newer is required", runs `brew upgrade git`, and
772	fetch/push/pull stay disabled with the toast still standing until they relaunch the app.
773	`refreshVCSToolReport` does re-run on every `apply(projects)`, but it gets the pinned answer back, and
774	dismissing the toast (`dismissedToolWarnings`) only hides it — nothing re-probes. `gh` got a monotonic
775	60s/10s TTL *and* a manual Refresh; the tool whose warning names an action the user is expected to go
776	perform got neither.
777	
778	Two structural gaps behind it, both fixed in `GitHubAuthCache` and both still live here:
779	
780	- **Reentrancy loses the single-flight and can downgrade the cache.** `await task.value` suspends the
781	  actor with `inFlight` set, and the `inFlight = nil` after it is unconditional and unstamped. A
782	  `probeJJ: false` caller finishing clears a concurrent `probeJJ: true` caller's slot, so the next jj
783	  caller forks a third `--version` pair; and if the jj-blind lane resumes *last* it overwrites the
784	  jj-aware report, because `probe(probeJJ: false)` returns `jj: .notInstalled` outright and
785	  `hasMissingTool(probedJJ: false)` doesn't count it. Narrow (both windows normally compute the same
786	  `probeJJ` from the same config) but exactly the class the `gh` generation stamp exists to kill.
787	- **`static let shared` plus an injected `runner:` is the hazard `GitHubAuthCache` documents rejecting**
